title: Business Lead
text: About Ramp Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $275B in annualized spend flows in and out of 85,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books. The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving. We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome. The median Ramp customer saves 7.5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same. If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it. About the Role As the Business Lead, you will be commercially responsible for the success of a new product at Ramp. The mandate is to do whatever it takes to grow the business. You will be expected to identify and resolve internal and external bottlenecks, often with limited guidance and support. You will set the strategy, prove out new bets, and influence how hundreds of go‑to‑market teammates sell and support the product. It’s an opportunity to run a “business within the business” at a meaningful scale while working directly with Ramp’s senior leadership. What You'll Do Set the strategy: Define the target customer, value proposition, pricing, packaging, and GTM approach. Own the plan and results: Set goals, measure progress, and take action when the things are off track. Drive cross-functional execution: Align stakeholders from different teams around clear priorities and goals. Own feedback loops: Work with customers and turn feedback into product and go-to-market changes. Build for scale : Identify resource needs, create repeatable processes, and transition mature work to the appropriate long-term teams. What You Need 5–10+ years in highly analytical, business‑driving roles A self-starter who will run through walls to get things done Exceptional analytical skills and command of data A systems thinker who understands how to build things that scale Strong communication skills and a team player Benefits available to all full-time Ramp employees (Global) Flexible PTO Centralized home-office equipment ordering Health and wellness stipend Budget for intra-office travel Weekly coffee stipend United States 100% medical, dental & vision insurance coverage for you, with partial coverage for dependents One Medical annual membership 401(k), including employer match on contributions made while employed by Ramp Fertility HRA (up to $10,000 per year) Parental leave: up to 16 weeks (birthing + bonding) or 8 weeks (bonding only) at 100% pay Pet insurance In-office perks: lunch, snacks, drinks, and more Relocation expense coverage to NYC or SF (if needed) Canada Group medical, dental, and vision coverage through Sun Life Life, AD&D, and disability coverage Fertility drug coverage (up to $4,000 lifetime) Group Retirement Plan with employer match (RRSP + DPSP) Parental leave: up to 16 weeks (birthing + bonding) or 8 weeks (bonding only) at 100% pay, with additional time available at reduced pay Employee Assistance Program and virtual care through Lumino Health United Kingdom Private medical insurance through Freedom Elite Virtual GP and at-home care via eMed x Livi Workplace pension through Penfold, with salary sacrifice option Parental leave: up to 16 weeks (birthing + bonding) or 8 weeks (bonding only) at 100% pay with additional time available at reduced pay Referral Instructions If you are being referred for the role, please contact that person to apply on your behalf. You will represent Product, Design and Engineering externally and will operate with deep conviction and understanding of Ramp’s technical capabilities. The role requires technical skills necessary to understand and educate on robust accounting features, and integrate them across all the touchpoints and surface area of a customer. This role is focused on Commercial and Mid-Market customers, supporting high-growth companies with standardized financial workflows, core ERP integrations, and repeatable implementation patterns that drive fast time-to-value. What You'll Do Act as a technical advisor to customers and Ramp’s internal teams while supporting high-value implementations and expansion opportunities by guiding integration, configuration, and system design Partner with Customer Activation and Account Management teams to assess customer requirements and propose scalable solutions; particularly involving ERP, HRIS, and API integrations Collaborate with onboarding specialists and implementation leads to support technical workstreams (not run them), ensuring faster time-to-value and customer success Work with customers to problem-solve technical hurdles and propose effective product implementations for each customer with a deep understanding of the full range of integration and configuration options Participate in technical discovery to understand customer systems and workflows, and recommend best-fit Ramp architecture. This includes when and how to use Ramp’s API Be a subject matter expert across our HRIS and Accounting integration partners, partnering with Sales, Product and partners to advocate for integration development in-line with customer needs Troubleshoot integration blockers and guide customers through complex configuration decisions without writing code directly Contribute to internal documentation and tooling that scales Ramp’s ability to support integration use cases across a growing customer base Influence Ramp’s product roadmap by channeling customer pain points and feedback to the Product and Engineering teams What You Need Bachelor's degree in computer science, engineering, finance, business, or a related field 2+ years in technical consulting, solutions engineering, implementation, or a similar customer-facing technical role, ideally in a SaaS or fintech environment Familiarity with ERP systems (e.g. NetSuite, Sage Intacct, Microsoft Dynamics, Oracle Fusion) and finance/accounting workflows. SAP S/4HANA or Sage Intacct expertise highly preferred. title: Customer Activation Manager | Enterprise
text: About Ramp Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $275B in annualized spend flows in and out of 85,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books. The median Ramp customer saves 7.5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same. If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it. About the Role Ramp's Enterprise CSMs don't manage accounts — they transform how companies run their finances. This is a role for people who have been inside large organizations when change was hard, who speak the language of a CFO, and who already use AI the way surgeons use instruments: not occasionally, not as an experiment, but as the default way they work. You'll be embedded in Ramp's enterprise accounts, responsible for driving genuine workflow transformation — not just onboarding completion. What You'll Do Lead enterprise customers through the full transformation journey — from implementation through agentic workflow adoption — with clear accountability for time-to-value and measurable business outcomes Build and own the change management strategy for each account: map stakeholders, diagnose resistance, build internal coalitions, and drive adoption past the finish line Quantify and communicate Ramp's impact in the language CFOs and Controllers care about — close cycle improvement, spend visibility, variance reduction, and ROI — not just product usage metrics Run executive-level stakeholder management across multiple layers of a customer org, including C-suite relationships you own independently Use AI tools daily to prepare for customer calls, build materials, synthesize data, identify account risk, and operate at a pace traditional methods can't match Help customers understand and adopt Ramp's agentic finance capabilities — positioning new workflows not as features, but as fundamental changes to how their finance team operates Partner with Account Executives and Technical Consulting to deliver seamless implementations and expand Ramp's footprint within accounts Bring customer insight back to Product — surfacing patterns, gaps, and opportunities from your accounts to shape how Ramp evolves About 30% travel expected Must-Haves Enterprise change management — You've driven workflow adoption inside complex organizations, navigated real resistance from real stakeholders, and have measurable results to show for it. Finance or fintech context is a plus but not required. ERP system fluency — You're comfortable working within and around major ERP platforms (NetSuite, SAP S/4HANA, Workday, Sage Intacct, or similar). You understand how these systems structure financial data, where integrations typically break, and how workflow changes ripple through an ERP-centric finance stack. This fluency is what lets you speak credibly to Controllers and finance ops teams about how Ramp fits into their existing systems of record. AI fluency as a daily habit — You already use AI tools habitually in your work. You use them to prep for calls, synthesize information, build customer-facing materials, and automate repetitive tasks. This is how you work, not something you're exploring. Ramp is a builder culture: if you don't instinctively reach for AI before doing things manually, this role will be a hard adjustment. Financial impact communication — You can walk a CFO through the business case for a workflow change, connect implementation milestones to P&L outcomes, and run executive updates in financial terms, not product terms. A finance background is not required — fluency is. Technical acumen — You can hold your own in conversations with Product and Engineering on integrations, APIs, and workflow architecture. You don't need to code, but credibility in technical conversations is what earns you a seat at the table with the full customer stakeholder group. 7+ years in enterprise customer success or implementations — You’ve spent enough time navigating complex organizations and senior stakeholders that it’s second nature. You know how to move an enterprise, not just support one. Nice-to-Haves Agentic workflow experience — You've helped customers adopt AI-powered or agentic workflows at scale. You understand what friction looks like in practice and what makes transformation actually stick. Finance domain depth — Exposure to FP&A, accounting software ecosystems (Netsuite, Sage, QuickBooks, Xero), expense management, or CFO-adjacent workflows. Accelerates credibility with Ramp's customer base. Demonstrated commercial impact — You can point to expansion, retention, or time-to-value outcomes with specific metrics attached — not described in general terms. Background at an AI-first or AI transformation company — not just a company that uses AI, but one where rethinking workflows around it was part of the product or culture High-growth or startup experience (comfort operating in ambiguity and rapid change) C-suite relationships built and maintained independently, without relying on a sales counterpart For candidates located in NYC or SF, the pay range for this role is $163,000 - $262,000. For candidates located in all other locations, the pay range for this role is $147,000- $236,000. About the Role Ramp is hiring a Lead Recruiter to own Director-level and above hiring across our G&A and business functions. You will lead some of the company’s most critical leadership searches, partnering directly with senior stakeholders to identify and hire leaders who will shape Ramp’s next stage of growth. You will own searches from initial scoping through close, partnering directly with executives and senior leaders across the business. You will be expected to develop real fluency in each area you support, translate ambiguous business needs into clear hiring strategies, and bring an independent point of view on talent. This is a hands-on role for someone who is equally strong at research, assessment, stakeholder partnership, and closing. You should be comfortable challenging assumptions, navigating sensitive and confidential searches, and creating structure without slowing the business down. You should be a self-starter who thrives in ambiguity, builds pipelines from scratch, and takes ownership of moving searches forward even when the role, target profile, or process is still taking shape. What You'll Do Own full-cycle recruiting for Director-level and above roles across G&A and business functions, from intake and market mapping through offer and close. Develop real fluency in the functions you support and quickly build context when taking on a new area, so you can identify the signals that distinguish exceptional leaders beyond title, company, and tenure. Build proactive pipelines through market research, targeted sourcing, referrals, and thoughtful engagement with passive candidates. Independently build momentum on confidential searches where broad outreach or an existing pipeline may not be available. Develop assessment approaches that surface a candidate’s leadership effectiveness, functional expertise, and ability to operate at Ramp’s pace and scale. Move fluidly across functions, evolving role definitions, and competing priorities while maintaining a consistently high bar for talent, execution, and candidate experience. Exercise discretion throughout sensitive searches, managing candidate information and stakeholder communication with sound judgment. What You Need 6+ years of full-cycle recruiting experience. A track record of independently leading complex senior-level searches from initial scoping through accepted offer. Ability to advise senior leaders, challenge requirements, and influence hiring decisions through clear communication, market insight, and data. Demonstrated ability to build fluency in unfamiliar functions, context-switch across very different searches, and maintain strong judgment as priorities and scope change. A high level of ownership and comfort with ambiguity. You can turn an open-ended business need into an actionable search, build a pipeline from scratch, and drive progress without waiting for direction. Strong closing skills, including experience navigating competing offers, senior candidates, and sensitive searches. Nice-to-Have Prior experience in executive search or a dedicated leadership recruiting role, particularly across G&A or business functions. Experience partnering directly with CEOs or other C-suite leaders on critical hires. Experience improving interview architecture, scorecards, market maps, or recruiting processes where structure was limited or still being built. Experience developing AI-enabled recruiting workflows that were adopted beyond your own individual searches. About Production Engineering Production Engineering is Ramp's infrastructure ownership layer. We exist to make Ramp faster, more reliable, and more scalable — and we do that by being embedded in the problems, not adjacent to them. A few things that define how we operate: One team, one company, one objective. There is no "infra team" and "product team" — there is Ramp. We share the company's goals as our own. When a product team struggles with reliability or scalability, that is our struggle. If reliability or scalability is at risk, we own it. We don't wait to be invited, and we don't ask whose code it is. If a system is slow, if it breaks, if it won't scale — that's ours to lead, regardless of where it lives in the stack. We go first, and we go fast. When the path isn't obvious, we don't wait for someone else to find it. We move with urgency, propose the solution, align the stakeholders, and stay in until it's done — not until our ticket is closed. We lead the way. We find the next problem before it finds us. And when we solve it, we don't just fix it for ourselves — the patterns and standards we establish become the foundation the rest of Ramp builds on. That's not a side effect of the job; it's the job. We stay calibrated. Speed means nothing if we're moving in the wrong direction. We regularly stop and ask honestly whether what we're working on is still the highest-leverage thing we could be doing — the discipline that makes sure our effort compounds toward what actually matters. You cannot build the future of finance on shaky infrastructure. Our Teams Production Engineering is organized into teams — but we think about teams differently. Teams are mutable. We build them around what needs to be done, not around what we need to do given the teams we already have. The structure below reflects our current priorities; it will evolve as Ramp does. Right now, we operate across four areas: Compute — the foundation everything runs on: container orchestration, networking, load balancing, edge infrastructure, and the deployment systems that get code from engineers' laptops to production reliably and at scale Storage — databases, caching, object storage, and the data infrastructure that underpins everything Workflows & Messaging — the systems that power Ramp's financial workflows and event-driven architecture Developer Infrastructure — the platform that makes every builder at Ramp faster and more autonomous: observability, cost attribution, and CI/CD systems that give teams visibility into what they build and what it costs What You'll Do Production Engineers at Ramp are full software engineers who happen to specialize in infrastructure . You write production code, you own systems end-to-end, and you drive technical outcomes across the organization — not just within your team. As a Tech Lead & Manager, you are a hands-on player-coach : you will lead and grow a team while remaining directly engaged in the technical work. Management at Ramp does not mean stepping away from the technology or the code. You will help set direction, develop engineers, and work alongside the team to deliver consequential infrastructure outcomes. Day to day, you will: Build, coach, and grow a high-performing team. Create clarity, give direct feedback, mentor engineers, and help each person expand their technical judgment, ownership, and leadership. Set technical direction for your team’s domain. Identify the highest-leverage problems, define a path forward, bring the right people along, and stay engaged with the team until the work is delivered. Build and operate critical infrastructure across Ramp's compute, storage, messaging, and observability stack — owning the systems that handle real financial transactions at scale. Drive architectural change — not just flag problems. When you surface a reliability or scalability issue, you own the path forward: you propose the solution, find the owners across engineering, and stay in until it's resolved. Partner with product teams at the design phase — reviewing architectures, embedding golden paths, and making it easy to build correctly the first time. Build Ramp's next level of scale — you'll be a hands-on contributor to the most consequential infrastructure shift happening right now: our move to a cellular architecture, enabling Ramp to scale, reach international markets, operate in highly regulated and constrained environments (e.g. FedRAMP), and deliver on enterprise-grade SLAs. Enable AI-native engineering — as Ramp builds increasingly AI-powered products, PE is the team that makes sure the platform can support them. You'll proactively partner with product teams on AI infrastructure patterns, define the golden paths that turn one-off solutions into reusable foundations, and stay ahead of emerging challenges before they become blockers. Build developer tooling and self-service infrastructure — so that other teams can answer their own questions (cost, performance, reliability) without involving PE. Participate in on-call rotation — and more importantly, use every incident as a signal to eliminate the root cause, not just resolve the symptom. Lead across the company — PE doesn't just review designs or show up when called. We proactively initiate cross-team architectural reviews, and we take full ownership of company-wide reliability and scalability initiatives: identifying the problem, proposing the solution, aligning the stakeholders, and staying in until it's done. What We Look For We don't hire for a checklist. We hire for the instincts that make someone exceptional on this team. The mindset we're looking for: You love building teams, mentoring engineers, and helping people grow—and you are equally energized by writing code, reviewing designs, and digging into complex distributed systems. You are a true player-coach. You know when to coach, delegate, and create space for others to lead; you also know when your direct technical involvement will create the most leverage. You can set a technical direction, bring people along, and then lock in with the team to make it happen. You do not believe managing engineers means stepping away from the technology or the code. You can't walk past something broken without wanting to fix it — and you don't stop at the workaround. You find the root cause and eliminate the class of problem. You think in systems, not tasks. You understand that "fixing the bug" is step one; making it so the bug can't happen again is the job. You move with urgency but without chaos. You know when to go fast and when to slow down and do it right. You treat product teams as your users. You build for them, communicate with them proactively, and measure success by how much faster they can ship. But you're also an owner — when something is broken or blocking, you don't wait to be asked. We win when our customers win. You leave things better than you found them. Every system you touch, every process you encounter — you move it forward. Not always dramatically, but always directionally. You picked it up in a certain state; you leave it in a better one. You are equally comfortable reading a database query plan, reviewing a system design doc, writing a Terraform module, and jumping into an incident at 2am. Experience profile: 8+ years of software engineering experience, including a track record of shipping high-quality architectures for critical systems. Staff+-level technical leadership: experience setting technical direction and leading complex, multi-quarter technical initiatives from ambiguous problems through durable production outcomes. Experience managing, mentoring, and developing engineers. You create clarity, give direct feedback, and help people grow in technical judgment, scope, and leadership. A sustained hands-on engineering track record. You are comfortable writing and reviewing production code, evaluating system designs, debugging incidents, and making difficult technical tradeoffs. Hands-on experience building and operating distributed systems at production scale. Strong software engineering fundamentals — you write clean, well-tested, production-ready code and set that standard for the team. Experience with at least one major cloud provider (AWS preferred). Familiarity with observability and reliability practices, including SLOs, error budgets, alerting, dashboards, and incident response. Track record of delivering through cross-functional coordination: aligning stakeholders, unblocking teams, and staying accountable for the outcome. Comfortable using AI tooling and coding agents as part of your everyday engineering workflow — and helping a team use them to move faster and think bigger. About the Role Ramp is building something ambitious, and we believe our most important advantage is our people. This role sits at the foundation of that belief. You'll help shape how Ramp identifies, evaluates, and hires world-class engineering talent, with a particular focus on the engineers at the center of what we're building next. This is a craft role. You'll own pipelines end-to-end, partner directly with our Engineering leadership, and be accountable for the quality of the people we bring through the door. We're looking for a Technical Recruiter who treats hiring as a discipline. Someone who cares as much about candidate experience and calibration as they do about closing. You won't just be working off a req list. We're looking for someone who can take ambiguous or high-level direction from engineering leadership and turn it into a sharp, targeted search, knowing exactly who they want before the role even opens. You'll be expected to have strong opinions on talent, defend them with evidence, and push back on stakeholders when the bar is at risk. Recruiting at Ramp is owned end-to-end, not handed off. This role requires someone who stays close to the candidate, close to the hiring manager, and close to the work, so context never gets lost between hand-offs. What You’ll Do Partner closely with our Engineering leadership and hiring managers to deeply understand the requirements of each role and how it fits into the organization Manage full-cycle recruiting for multiple, complex searches across our Engineering organization, owning every stage from first touch to signed offer Build deeply targeted sourcing strategies. Know the companies, the teams, and the individual engineers worth pursuing before opening a search Partner with our sourcing team to iterate on creative strategies for talent pipelines and competitor mapping Run candidate process with urgency and care. Same-day follow-up, next steps booked before you hang up, no candidate left chasing us Manage pipeline activity, maintain data integrity, and proactively share data-centric updates with internal stakeholders. Spot funnel issues early and bring evidence to calibration conversations, not just gut Drive offer processes for candidates, including extending offers, negotiations, closing candidates, and generating offer letters Act as a strategic advisor, not a req-filler. Anticipate hiring needs, shape strategy alongside engineering stakeholders, and translate abstract asks into concrete target lists, comp frameworks, and close plans Lead initiatives that raise the bar on how technical recruiting operates at Ramp, including interview loops, interviewer training, scorecards, and other cross-functional efforts that increase hiring quality and speed Build excellent relationships across the recruiting team and your engineering client groups What We’re Looking For 5+ years of full-cycle technical recruiting/sourcing experience in a similar role at a high-growth technology company or startup Demonstrated track record hiring for deeply technical engineering roles. If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it. About the Role We’re looking for a Senior Business Systems Engineer to own and evolve Ramp’s Quote-to-Cash systems. You’ll build and maintain Ramp’s Salesforce-based quoting platform, contract workflows, and Billing/Core integrations that turn complex commercial agreements into accurate, supportable customer outcomes—from quote creation and approvals through order forms, provisioning, billing, renewals, and amendments. This is not a Salesforce CPQ implementation role. Ramp uses an in-house Quote-to-Cash platform built on Salesforce, so we’re looking for a strong Salesforce engineer with experience in quoting, pricing, contracts, billing, subscriptions, or other complex commercial workflows. This role sits in Growth Engineering’s Business Systems Engineering team and partners closely with Deal Desk, Legal, Finance, Billing Engineering, Product, and GTM teams. You’ll combine hands-on Salesforce engineering with systems design and strong commercial judgment to make high-stakes revenue workflows reliable, scalable, and easier for teams to use. What You’ll Do Design, develop, test, and deploy applications on the Salesforce Platform. Design, build, and operate Ramp’s Salesforce-based Quote-to-Cash platform and the integrations between Salesforce, Ironclad, Billing/Core, and adjacent business systems. Own data contracts, idempotency, error handling, reconciliation, and safe lifecycle changes for quotes, contracts, and subscriptions. Design, develop, and maintain integration solutions using in-house services and approved automation platforms. Drive architecture, tooling, and design decisions that keep commercial systems fast, reliable, and scalable. Write and communicate technical specifications, including architecture diagrams, data models, process flows, and sequence diagrams. Own data integrity and the operating assumptions for your domain; continually improve them. Partner with the rest of the team on code reviews, operational support, debugging, and solution design. What You’ll Need 7+ years building applications on the Salesforce Platform. 5+ years of systems architecture and integration experience. Strong hands-on experience with Apex, triggers, Lightning Web Components, Flows, and asynchronous processing. Working knowledge of another programming language, such as Python. Strong API and integration-design skills, including reliable handling of retries, duplicate events, partial failures, and data reconciliation. Experience with Quote-to-Cash domains such as quoting, pricing, approvals, contract lifecycle management, billing, subscriptions, renewals, or amendments. Experience with Salesforce CPQ is welcome but not required. Familiarity with the broader GTM stack beyond Salesforce, such as Gong, LeanData, contract lifecycle management, billing, or revenue systems. Strong knowledge of synchronous and asynchronous integration patterns, streaming APIs, and publish/subscribe architectures. Working knowledge of data pipelines, CI/CD, Salesforce platform limits, code coverage, and unit-testing practices. Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to translate complex commercial requirements into simple, durable system behavior with non-engineering partners. Experience using AI-assisted development tools thoughtfully and evaluating their output. text: About Ramp Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $275B in annualized spend flows in and out of 85,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books. The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving. We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. The median Ramp customer saves 7.5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same. If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it. About the Role How we build software is changing. Designers are building tools and agents, prototyping in code, and shipping directly into the product. More people can create software than ever before. That makes design judgment more important, not less. We’re looking for a Design Systems Lead to build that judgment into the foundations of Ramp. This is not just about maintaining a component library. It’s about making it possible for designers, engineers, and agents to build experiences that look, feel, and work like Ramp—without a designer driving every decision or the design systems team reviewing every change. You’re a designer first, with the technical depth to guide architecture and get into the code. You have exceptional taste and strong opinions about typography, hierarchy, interaction, and motion. Just as importantly, you know how to turn that judgment into patterns, tools, and guidance that make everyone else’s work better. You’re deeply curious about AI and already using it to change how you work. You build, experiment, inspect the results, and push past the demo. You can imagine a different way of building software—and lead a team toward it. This role is for you if you’re excited by: Making great design reproducible. Raise the quality of Ramp’s product and encode what makes it good, so people and agents can produce coherent, usable experiences by default. The system should make excellent work easier, not make every experience look the same. Reimagining what a design system can be. Build beyond components and tokens into composition, interaction patterns, agent guidance, and evaluations. Connect exploration and production so the fastest way to build is also a path to great quality. Leading a team that multiplies everyone else’s impact. Create clear direction, ambitious goals, and a caring yet demanding environment. Inspire curiosity, develop people, and stay close enough to the work to help make it exceptional. The opportunity is to raise the floor for everyone building at Ramp, while giving designers more room to make the most important experiences extraordinary. What You'll Do Lead and develop the design systems team. Set clear priorities, ownership, and goals. Give direct, timely feedback, hold people accountable, and help them do the best work of their careers. Own the system’s vision and direction. Decide what to preserve, evolve, simplify, or replace based on what builders and customers need. Turn that direction into focused work the team can deliver. Elevate Ramp’s visual and interaction design. Raise the bar for typography, hierarchy, density, motion, responsive behavior, accessibility, and the states beyond the happy path. Make design judgment usable by people and agents. Translate principles into reusable patterns, reference experiences, composition rules, and guidance that produce better work without you in the room. Guide technical architecture with engineering. Shape everything from components and tokens to how agents discover guidance, compose interfaces, and check their work. Make sound tradeoffs between flexibility, coherence, performance, and ease of use. Stay hands-on. Build prototypes, work in code, and get into implementation details to test ideas, unblock the team, and understand where the system breaks down. Define and measure quality. Build repeatable evaluations grounded in real tasks. Measure whether builders can ship better work faster, with less rework—not just whether they use the tools. About Production Engineering Production Engineering is Ramp's infrastructure ownership layer. We exist to make Ramp faster, more reliable, and more scalable — and we do that by being embedded in the problems, not adjacent to them. A few things that define how we operate: One team, one company, one objective. There is no "infra team" and "product team" — there is Ramp. We share the company's goals as our own. When a product team struggles with reliability or scalability, that is our struggle. If reliability or scalability is at risk, we own it. We don't wait to be invited, and we don't ask whose code it is. If a system is slow, if it breaks, if it won't scale — that's ours to lead, regardless of where it lives in the stack. We go first, and we go fast. When the path isn't obvious, we don't wait for someone else to find it. We move with urgency, propose the solution, align the stakeholders, and stay in until it's done — not until our ticket is closed. We lead the way. We find the next problem before it finds us. And when we solve it, we don't just fix it for ourselves — the patterns and standards we establish become the foundation the rest of Ramp builds on. That's not a side effect of the job; it's the job. We stay calibrated. Speed means nothing if we're moving in the wrong direction. We regularly stop and ask honestly whether what we're working on is still the highest-leverage thing we could be doing — the discipline that makes sure our effort compounds toward what actually matters. You cannot build the future of finance on shaky infrastructure. Our Teams Production Engineering is organized into teams — but we think about teams differently. Teams are mutable. We build them around what needs to be done, not around what we need to do given the teams we already have. The structure below reflects our current priorities; it will evolve as Ramp does. Right now, we operate across four areas: Compute — the foundation everything runs on: container orchestration, networking, load balancing, edge infrastructure, and the deployment systems that get code from engineers' laptops to production reliably and at scale Storage — databases, caching, object storage, and the data infrastructure that underpins everything Workflows & Messaging — the systems that power Ramp's financial workflows and event-driven architecture Internal Infrastructure — the platform that makes every builder at Ramp faster and more autonomous: observability, cost attribution, and CI/CD systems that give teams visibility into what they build and what it costs What You'll Do Production Engineers at Ramp are full software engineers who happen to specialize in infrastructure . You write production code, you own systems end-to-end, and you drive technical outcomes across the organization — not just within your team. Day to day, you will: Build and operate critical infrastructure across Ramp's compute, storage, messaging, and observability stack — owning the systems that handle real financial transactions at scale. Drive architectural change — not just flag problems. When you surface a reliability or scalability issue, you own the path forward: you propose the solution, find the owners across engineering, and stay in until it's resolved. Partner with product teams at the design phase — reviewing architectures, embedding golden paths, and making it easy to build correctly the first time. Build Ramp's next level of scale — you'll be a hands-on contributor to the most consequential infrastructure shift happening right now: our move to a cellular architecture, enabling Ramp to scale, reach international markets, operate in highly regulated and constrained environments (e.g. FedRAMP), and deliver on enterprise-grade SLAs. Enable AI-native engineering — as Ramp builds increasingly AI-powered products, PE is the team that makes sure the platform can support them. You'll proactively partner with product teams on AI infrastructure patterns, define the golden paths that turn one-off solutions into reusable foundations, and stay ahead of emerging challenges before they become blockers. Build developer tooling and self-service infrastructure — so that other teams can answer their own questions (cost, performance, reliability) without involving PE. Participate in on-call rotation — and more importantly, use every incident as a signal to eliminate the root cause, not just resolve the symptom. Lead across the company — PE doesn't just review designs or show up when called. We proactively initiate cross-team architectural reviews, and we take full ownership of company-wide reliability and scalability initiatives: identifying the problem, proposing the solution, aligning the stakeholders, and staying in until it's done. What We Look For We don't hire for a checklist. We hire for the instincts that make someone exceptional on this team. The mindset we're looking for: You can't walk past something broken without wanting to fix it — and you don't stop at the workaround. You find the root cause and eliminate the class of problem. You think in systems, not tasks. You understand that "fixing the bug" is step one; making it so the bug can't happen again is the job. You move with urgency but without chaos. You know when to go fast and when to slow down and do it right. You treat product teams as your users. You build for them, communicate with them proactively, and measure success by how much faster they can ship. But you're also an owner — when something is broken or blocking, you don't wait to be asked. We win when our customers win. You leave things better than you found them. Every system you touch, every process you encounter — you move it forward. Not always dramatically, but always directionally. You picked it up in a certain state; you leave it in a better one. You are equally comfortable reading a database query plan, reviewing a system design doc, writing a Terraform module, and jumping into an incident at 2am. About the Role Most businesses have no idea if they're overpaying for their software. They renew on autopilot, negotiate without benchmarks, and discover vendor alternatives only after the contract is already signed. Ramp is uniquely positioned to change that. We see billions of dollars of real-world spend and contract data across thousands of companies, and we're turning it into an intelligence layer that tells businesses exactly what they should be paying, which vendors to consider, and when to act. As PM for Vendor Intelligence & Marketplace, you'll own the product that powers this: our price benchmarking engine, contract analysis (extracting structure and risk from vendor agreements), and the emerging B2B marketplace that connects Ramp's buyer base to the right vendors at the right price. You'll be one of the first PMs building a true buyer-side intelligence layer inside a financial platform, replacing renewal anxiety and negotiation guesswork with data-driven, AI-powered decisions. Please note that this role requires in-person presence at our NYC or SF office at least 2 days/week. What You’ll Do Own the strategy and roadmap for price benchmarks and contract intelligence, turning Ramp's aggregated spend and contract dataset into the most accurate price benchmarking product on the market. Build the B2B marketplace primitives that let Ramp's customers discover, compare, and engage with the right vendors, and give vendors a channel to reach Ramp's buyer base with transparent, competitive pricing. Design "decision moments": surfaces inside Ramp that deliver the right benchmark, contract context, or vendor alternative at exactly the moment a customer is about to sign, renew, or spend. Partner with data science to build the extraction, normalization, and modeling pipelines that power price benchmarks, going from raw contract PDFs and spend data to unit-normalized, SKU-level intelligence a customer can act on in a negotiation. Define the evaluation methodology, quality bar, and feedback loops for AI-powered contract analysis, ensuring the accuracy and explainability that enterprise customers require. Cover the full vendor lifecycle: discovery and intake through price negotiation, contract signing, and renewal, with the right intelligence surfaced at each step. Develop deep understanding of how procurement, finance, and legal teams evaluate, select, and renegotiate vendors, and translate that into sharp product bets with clear customer outcomes. Drive cross-functional alignment on dependencies and launch readiness: GTM enablement, customer communications, compliance review, and supportability. What You Need BA/BS in a technical or analytical field (Computer Science, Engineering, Analytics, Mathematics, Economics, or related). 5+ years of product management experience, ideally with products where data quality and customer trust are the core value proposition. Sharp product judgment on data products and marketplaces: you understand flywheel dynamics, network effects, coverage-versus-accuracy tradeoffs, and the cold-start problem. AI fluency: hands-on experience building AI features, comfort with LLM-based extraction and retrieval, evaluation methodology, and human-in-the-loop design. Strong commercial instincts: you understand how businesses buy software, what levers drive negotiation outcomes, and why price transparency changes behavior. Track record building products where trust is earned over time: explainability, auditability, graceful degradation, and clear user controls. Comfort working in technical environments (Figma, SQL, Git) and prototyping quickly with modern AI tools (Claude Code, Cursor). Clear, direct communication across technical and non-technical stakeholders; ability to make a crisp case for a product bet without a deck full of slides. Nice-to-Haves Experience building price benchmarking, market intelligence, or contract analytics products, anywhere from procurement software to B2B SaaS to fintech. Marketplace experience: supply/demand matching, seller acquisition, buyer discovery, and the trust primitives that make two-sided systems work. Document understanding: OCR, LLM-based extraction, normalizing structured data from unstructured contracts. Background in procurement, vendor management, or enterprise SaaS buying and selling, either as a PM or as a practitioner. Familiarity with compliance-adjacent domains: vendor due diligence, security reviews, NDAs, audit trails. Experience at a high-growth startup taking 0→1 products to scale. You will learn a complex product deeply enough to troubleshoot across payments, bank linking, accounting syncs, and card programs, then partner with teams across Engineering, Risk, Product, and Partnerships to get problems solved. What You’ll Do Be the voice of Ramp's Customer Support. You'll spend your day engaging with customers, primarily via live calls, email, and chat. Diagnose across a broad product surface. Ramp isn't one product — it's payments, cards, travel, accounting integrations, and more. You'll need to understand how they connect and where they break. Operate with an ownership mindset, managing escalations end-to-end. You take full accountability for every ticket you handle. When an issue crosses team boundaries — risk, engineering, product, partnerships — you route it correctly, follow up, and make sure the customer isn't left waiting. You'll work across Zendesk, internal tooling, and Slack-based escalation workflows. Build and shape AI tools, not just use them. Ramp is building AI into CX operations. You'll use AI-powered research tools and proprietary tools like Glass daily, provide direct feedback on what's working, and play an active role in how these tools evolve. You're not just a user — you're a builder. We are all builders at Ramp. Ship improvements, not just flag them. When you notice a process gap, a missing SOP, or a knowledge base article that's sending associates down the wrong path, you don't just raise it — you have the autonomy to roll up your sleeves and fix it. Leverage AI to solve problems, build automations, and improve the systems around you. The best people in this role make the whole team better. Communicate with precision and empathy. Our customers are financially sophisticated. You need to explain what's happening, what you're doing about it, and what they should expect — clearly and without filler. What You Need You're a systems thinker: you don't just solve the ticket in front of you, you ask why the problem exists and how to prevent it from happening again. You actively use AI tools — Claude, Notion AI, research and workflow tools — and can demonstrate how you've applied them to get real work done. This is a hard requirement. You're fast-moving while holding yourself to a high bar for execution: you balance speed, accuracy, and thoroughness in every interaction. You can hold a technical conversation about how systems connect (APIs, bank integrations, accounting software) even if you're not writing code. You manage competing priorities without dropping things. When you have 15 open issues across 4 internal teams, nothing falls through. You write clearly and concisely. You can explain a payment reconciliation issue to a CFO without jargon. You're comfortable on the phone. Many interactions start there. You have a demonstrated track record of exceeding key performance standards, including CSAT, QA, and speed-of-service metrics. You work directly with Product, Engineering, and GTM teams — not siloed into a support queue. AI tools and unlimited access. Unlimited tokens, proprietary AI tools like Glass, and a culture that expects you to use them to move faster and build smarter. Career growth that you own. Grow within CX, explore other functions internally, or carve out a path that doesn't exist yet. If you're invested, we're invested. Culture that's different from a call center. Team events, in-person offsites, and a genuine commitment to building a team people want to be part of. Our customers rely on us to keep their operations running: invoices get paid, books get closed, and finance leaders can trust the data behind every decision. In this role, you will be the person who spots where customers are getting stuck and drives issues to a clear resolution. You will learn a complex product deeply enough to troubleshoot across payments, bank linking, accounting syncs, and card programs, then partner with teams across Engineering, Risk, Product, and Partnerships to get problems solved. This is not script-based support. You will triage, investigate, and make high-signal judgment calls throughout the day. You will thrive in this role if you are a systems thinker and deeply customer obsessed. Support is the baseline. How you think about improving processes, tools, and outcomes is what sets you apart. What You’ll Do Be the voice of Ramp's Customer Support. You'll spend your day engaging with customers, primarily via live calls, email, and chat. Diagnose across a broad product surface. Ramp isn't one product — it's payments, cards, travel, accounting integrations, and more. You'll need to understand how they connect and where they break. Operate with an ownership mindset, managing escalations end-to-end. You take full accountability for every ticket you handle. When an issue crosses team boundaries — risk, engineering, product, partnerships — you route it correctly, follow up, and make sure the customer isn't left waiting. You'll work across Zendesk, internal tooling, and Slack-based escalation workflows. Build and shape AI tools, not just use them. Ramp is building AI into CX operations. You'll use AI-powered research tools and proprietary tools like Glass daily, provide direct feedback on what's working, and play an active role in how these tools evolve. You're not just a user — you're a builder. We are all builders at Ramp. Ship improvements, not just flag them. When you notice a process gap, a missing SOP, or a knowledge base article that's sending associates down the wrong path, you don't just raise it — you have the autonomy to roll up your sleeves and fix it. Leverage AI to solve problems, build automations, and improve the systems around you. The best people in this role make the whole team better. Communicate with precision and empathy. Our customers are financially sophisticated. You need to explain what's happening, what you're doing about it, and what they should expect — clearly and without filler. What You Need You're a systems thinker: you don't just solve the ticket in front of you, you ask why the problem exists and how to prevent it from happening again. You actively use AI tools — Claude, Notion AI, research and workflow tools — and can demonstrate how you've applied them to get real work done. This is a hard requirement. You're fast-moving while holding yourself to a high bar for execution: you balance speed, accuracy, and thoroughness in every interaction. You can hold a technical conversation about how systems connect (APIs, bank integrations, accounting software) even if you're not writing code. You manage competing priorities without dropping things. When you have 15 open issues across 4 internal teams, nothing falls through. You write clearly and concisely. You can explain a payment reconciliation issue to a CFO without jargon. You're comfortable on the phone. Many interactions start there. You have a demonstrated track record of exceeding key performance standards, including CSAT, QA, and speed-of-service metrics. Nice to Haves Experience building workflows or automations using AI tools, not just prompting Familiarity with accounting workflows (AP/AR, GL, reconciliation) or ERP integrations (NetSuite, QuickBooks, Sage) Background in payments infrastructure (ACH, wire transfers, card networks) Track record of working somewhere that shipped product fast and expected CX to keep up Why be a CX Associate at Ramp Cross-functional exposure from day one. You work directly with Product, Engineering, and GTM teams — not siloed into a support queue. AI tools and unlimited access. Unlimited tokens, proprietary AI tools like Glass, and a culture that expects you to use them to move faster and build smarter. Career growth that you own. Grow within CX, explore other functions internally, or carve out a path that doesn't exist yet. If you're invested, we're invested. Culture that's different from a call center. Team events, in-person offsites, and a genuine commitment to building a team people want to be part of. Read more about how Ramp thinks about AI and CX: How Ramp Became an AI-First Company — Geoff Charles, CPO Inside Glass: How Ramp Built a Proprietary AI Platform for CX — Seb Goddijn, AI Product Manager AI-Powered Customer Experience at Ramp — Ben Levick, Head of CX / Ramp AI What to know before you apply Schedule & Shift Bidding - Please Read Carefully: CX Associates work a set 40-hour/week schedule assigned through a schedule-bid process. Working hours span 7:00 AM–11:00 PM ET , and your shift will likely include a weekend day (either Sun–Thu or Tue–Sat ). Associates also cover 2–3 company holidays per year on a rotating basis. Ramp's customers operate on financial deadlines that don't pause. The product changes frequently. If you need a stable, predictable environment, this isn't it. The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving. We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome. The median Ramp customer saves 7.5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same. If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it. About the Role Ramp believes that AI-powered CX organizations are the future and we are racing to build the best one in the world. Our goal is for our team to work hand in hand with AI agents to drive superlative customer outcomes and the highest-velocity AI improvement engine in the business. This role will own the strategy and ops teams that are making that transition a reality while still delivering 24/7/365 support for our 85,000+ customers every day. You will work with the Head of CX to set the goals, measure what matters, and build the systems and programs that push the team forward. You’ll manage a small and mighty team across Business Operations, CX Analytics, Workforce Management, Learning & Development, and CX AI Operations to accomplish your goals. We believe every CX frontline specialist has a role to play driving forward the performance of our AI agents - it is not work reserved for a dedicated AI team. Each specialist needs to be trained, coached, scheduled, and rewarded for continuous work of closing AI learning loops, ensuring AI escalations get resolved, and obsessing about how our customers are actually being served. You'll do this while running a global support operation that has to be excellent today. Once we nail the model in CX, there will be momentum to help other operations teams adopt it. What You’ll Do Set the goals and measure what matters. Work with the Head of CX and senior CX managers to set org-wide goals, decide how we measure progress, and deliver the programs and projects that enable that strategy to flourish. Define how specialists and AI agents work together. Build the roles, workflows, and expectations that let specialists and AI agents serve customers as one team. Change what we reward. Rebuild goals, incentives, and performance management so specialists get credit for closing AI learning loops, getting AI escalations resolved, and improving how customers are actually served, alongside traditional frontline performance. Own global schedules, capacity, and quality. Plan coverage for 24/7/365, multi-tier, global support that holds a high bar for customers of all shapes and sizes. Build the training model for the new work. Both new and tenured specialists need to investigate hard issues, judge agent behavior, and contribute fixes, while still developing a deep understanding Ramp’s complex financial products. L&D should make them good at all of it. Turn AI progress into operating change. Know what our Investigative Copilot (specialist-facing) and AskRamp (fully agentic) can do and how well they do it. When that moves, change staffing, workflows, training, and expectations to match. Build and own the voice of the CX specialist to Product and Engineering. Use CX data to show technical teams where agents succeed and where they struggle, and work with them directly on tooling, prompts, and agent behavior. They own the roadmap; you make sure CX's evidence shapes it. Build a small, strong team. Develop and grow leaders across Business Operations, CX Analytics, Workforce Management, Learning & Development, and CX AI Operations, with clear ownership and shared goals. What We’re Looking For We want an operator who has already changed how real work gets done with AI and can show the results. A record of strategic and operational execution inside an operating unit or fast growth business . That could be CX, Sales, supply chain, or another function where you owned the goals, the systems, and the outcomes. A genuine AI transformation you were on the front lines of in the last 18-24 months. You changed how a team’s work gets done and kept it running in production. You can explain what improved, what failed, and what you learned. Exceptional intellectual horsepower and natural curiosity , demonstrated through outstanding, standout performance across past roles in demanding environments. Experience leading teams and developing reports , with sound judgment about organizational design, incentives, and performance management. Analytical depth you use yourself: you can build or audit a capacity model, challenge a metric, diagnose an operating problem, or review an AI agent session to find the flaws. Credibility with Product, Engineering, and Data teams , and the ability to shape their priorities without a reporting line. High standards for customer quality and human accountability - you don’t compromise on the customer outcome. Helpful Experience Leadership spanning business operations, CX analytics, workforce management, learning and development, or AI operations or their equivalents in other operating teams. Experience with production AI agents, evaluations, escalation workflows, and continuous improvement. Taking an operating model that worked in one team and making it successful elsewhere. How Success Will Be Measured Specialists and AI agents work as one team, measured through both direct frontline performance as well as agentic velocity. Every specialist is trained, coached, scheduled, and rewarded for migrating successfully into an AI native version of the role. Learning loops close fast, AI escalations produce durable fixes, and new agent capabilities show up as operational gains. Customer quality goes up and 24/7/365 support stays excellent while the operating model changes. Other Ramp operations teams are adopting what worked in CX. Compensation For candidates located in New York City or San Francisco, the base salary range for this role is $184,000–$250,000. For candidates located in all other locations, the base salary range will be between $175,000-$220,000. title: デリバリーソリューションアーキテクト
text: Req ID: CSQ427R266 Location: Tokyo, Japan Databricksは、お客様がAIプラットフォームを活用して、世界で最も難しいなデータに関する課題を解決できるよう支援することをミッションとしています。デリバリーソリューションアーキテクト（DSA）は、この重要なミッションにおいて、セールスおよびフィールド・エンジニアリングチームと協力し、お客様のDatabricksプラットフォームの導入と利用拡大を加速させる重要な役割を担います。DSAとして、お客様がすでに導入を決定したDatabricksのワークロードについて、お客様がプラットフォームから最大限の価値と投資対効果を得られるよう、技術的な指導とサポートを提供し、お客様の成功を確実にします。特に、複雑な課題を抱えるお客様に対して、より重点的かつ技術的な責任を持って支援を行います。 このポジションは、技術とビジネスの両面を兼ね備えたハイブリッドな役割です。担当するお客様とユースケースにおいて、成長を推進します。ビジネス面では、お客様の意思決定者と関係を構築し、他の専門チームと連携しながら、Databricksが実行できる計画や戦略を策定・推進します。技術面ではDatabricksの全製品における、お客様導入後の技術的なリーダーとなります。組織内のあらゆるレベルの人々と、技術的な専門知識を活かしてコミュニケーションをとる能力が求められます。 あなたがもたらす影響 : 戦略的アカウントにおける複雑なユースケースおよび複数のワークストリーム全体で、技術的な実行戦略を定義し、影響を与える。 お客様のテクニカルリードやアーキテクトにとって信頼される技術アドバイザーとなり、アーキテクチャの議論をリードし、技術的な意思決定をガイドする。 パフォーマンス、コスト、信頼性、長期的なニーズのバランスを取りながら、安全かつガバナンスの効いたスケーラブルなDatabricksアーキテクチャを設計する。 お客様の成果を加速させる実用的なソリューション、プロトタイプ、再利用可能な技術資産を構築・実証する。 プラットフォームの成熟度とスケーリングのニーズを予測し、セキュリティ、ガバナンス、運用の卓越性に関するベストプラクティスを確立する。 アーキテクチャに影響を与え、デリバリーの障害を取り除き、技術的な実行をビジネス成果に結びつけることで、プラットフォームの採用と利用を促進する。 Databricks、お客様、導入チームと連携し、リソースの調整、リスク管理、デリバリーの加速を行う。 同僚を指導し、組織全体で活用できる再利用可能な技術ガイダンス、フレームワーク、およびイネーブルメントに貢献する。 必要な条件/経験: ソリューションアーキテクト、ソリューションエンジニアリング、技術コンサルティング、プロフェッショナルサービス、データエンジニアリング、または関連する技術的役割における5年以上の経験 複雑な顧客のユースケースや複数のワークストリーム全体で、技術戦略やアーキテクチャに影響を与えた経験 Python、SQL、または類似の言語における高いコーディング能力と、技術的ソリューションの構築、デバッグ、検証を行う能力 分散データシステム、データエンジニアリング、分析、データウェアハウジング、AI/ML、および最新のクラウドアーキテクチャに関する深い理解 安全でガバナンスが効き、スケーラブルかつ本番環境に対応したデータソリューションを設計した経験 不明確な技術的問題を解決し、トレードオフを評価し、構造化された分析や実験を通じてソリューションを検証する能力 技術リード、アーキテクト、および顧客のシニアステークホルダーとのアーキテクチャ議論をリードした経験 セキュリティ、ガバナンス、パフォーマンス、信頼性、コスト最適化など、プラットフォームの運用上の卓越性に関する深い理解 技術的リーダーシップを通じて、顧客の採用、利用、そして測定可能なビジネス成果を促進した実績 強力なステークホルダーマネジメントおよび部門横断的なリーダーシップスキル（正式な権限なしでチームを調整する能力を含む） コンピュータサイエンス、工学、または同等の分野における学士号 日本語の完全な専門的習熟度が必須 望ましい経験/スキル Databricksの経験または認定資格 AI/ML、データエンジニアリング、ストリーミング、データウェアハウジング、ガバナンス、マイグレーションなどの技術分野における専門知識の構築 AWS、Azure、またはGCPおよび本番環境でのクラウドデプロイメントの経験 チーム全体で活用できる、再利用可能な技術フレームワーク、デモ、またはイネーブルメント（支援策）を作成した経験 ビジネスレベルの英語力があれば尚可 選考プロセス: title: Account Executive - Strategic Core
text: SLSQ128R22 As a Strategic Core Account Executive, your mission will be to lead the executive relationship, overall consumption growth, and cross-enterprise expansion across a select group of Databricks’ largest strategic accounts in Korea. This role is centered on expanding our strategic footprint within complex conglomerates and large enterprises. You will position Databricks as the enterprise-wide standard for data, analytics, and generative AI by identifying new buying centers, driving multi-million-dollar commitments, and accelerating workload consumption. Working as the general manager of your named accounts, you will orchestrate specialized cross-functional teams, executive sponsors, and global partners to unlock mission-critical customer transformations. You will report to the Director of Sales, Korea. The impact you will have: Own and grow total annual contract value (ACV), consumption revenue, and customer lifetime value within a dedicated portfolio of Korea's largest strategic enterprise accounts. Build and execute multi-year strategic account plans that align Databricks capabilities directly with the customer’s strategic transformation roadmaps. Systematically uncover new buying centers and business units across corporate subsidiaries, expanding adoption from initial workloads to company-wide standardization. Build and maintain C-level and board-level relationships across both technology and business functions (CEO, CIO, CDO, BU Presidents). Drive widespread consumption growth by collaborating with customer success, forward-deployed engineering, and professional services teams. Lead complex commercial negotiations, long-term multi-year enterprise license agreements, and consumption commit structures. Coordinate deeply with strategic global and domestic SI partners and Hyperscalers (AWS, Azure, GCP) to deliver mission-critical solutions at enterprise scale. What we look for: 10+ years of experience in enterprise technology sales, managing top-tier named accounts or conglomerate groups in Korea. Proven track record of closing 8-figure / multi-million-dollar complex cloud, PaaS, or enterprise software agreements. Deep expertise in consumption-based business models, workload migration, and cloud/data modernization. title: Accounting Data & Technology Manager
location: Mountain View, California; San Francisco, California
text: GAQ327R291 Accounting Data & Technology Manager About the Role We are building a finance function that stays ahead of the curve — leveraging AI, automation, and modern tooling to operate at the pace Databricks demands. We are seeking an Accounting Data & Technology Manager to join our Global Accounting team and serve as the architect of the redesign of our accounting processes by building automation solutions and managing data pipelines that power our global accounting organization. You will serve as the accounting team's S/4HANA expert — the person who ensures our in-flight SAP implementation reflects best practice rather than a lift-and-shift of how we operate in NetSuite today. You will be responsible for bridging the gap between our team's subject matter experts, our technology solutions, and the business data needed to support accounting operations. In addition to SAP ownership, this role will build purposeful, reliable solutions on top of the Databricks platform and Finance Datalake to accelerate global accounting operations. During the SAP implementation, you will work alongside our system integrator to challenge design decisions, identify where SAP's native capabilities can replace manual workarounds, and ensure the accounting team is building on the right foundation from day one. Post go-live, the role transitions to continuous improvement — owning automation opportunities, streamlining close processes as SAP capabilities evolve, and ensuring Databricks is getting progressively more value out of the platform over time rather than running it as a static system. This is a rare opportunity to shape a major ERP platform from day one at one of the world's fastest-growing technology companies, with the autonomy to define how SAP works for accounting at Databricks — and how it connects to the most advanced data and AI platform in the market. What You'll Do SAP Implementation Governance (Near-Term) Work alongside our system integrator as the accounting team's internal SAP S/4HANA subject matter expert throughout the implementation program. Challenge design decisions and configuration choices — ensuring they reflect SAP best practice rather than replicating current-state NetSuite processes. Identify where SAP's native capabilities (standard workflows, automated postings, embedded analytics, Fiori apps) can replace manual workarounds and custom development. Own the accounting team's requirements, testing, and sign-off for SAP configuration across core FICO areas — general ledger, accounts payable, accounts receivable, fixed assets, and close management. Partner with our system integrator, IT and Finance Transformation to ensure data migration, chart of accounts design, and master data governance meet accounting's needs. Continuous Improvement & Optimization (Post Go-Live) Own the SAP continuous improvement roadmap for accounting — identifying automation opportunities, process simplifications, and new SAP capabilities as they are released. Streamline close processes within SAP — driving adoption of native automation, reducing cycle time, eliminating manual steps, and improving data quality with each close cycle. Monitor system performance and proactively address configuration issues, data quality gaps, and process bottlenecks. Collaborate with Tax, Treasury, FP&A, Accounts Payable, Revenue, and Procurement to ensure SAP configuration supports end-to-end finance processes — not just accounting in isolation. Ensure SOX-relevant system controls (automated, access and change management controls) within SAP are properly configured, documented, and operating effectively. SAP × Databricks Platform Integration Own the design and governance of how SAP accounting data flows into the Databricks Data Intelligence Platform — ensuring clean, timely, and well-structured data for financial reporting, analytics, and AI use cases. Partner with Data Engineering and Finance Systems to define the SAP-to-Databricks integration architecture — including extraction patterns, data models, and refresh cadences that support close timelines and ad-hoc analysis. Identify opportunities to leverage Databricks' AI and automation capabilities on top of SAP data — such as anomaly detection on journal entries, predictive accruals, automated reconciliation matching, and natural-language reporting via Genie. Serve as the accounting team's voice in shaping how Databricks' own platform is used for internal finance operations — ensuring the company is a best-practice reference customer for its own technology. What We're Looking For Required Qualifications 8+ years of progressive experience in accounting systems, ERP administration, or finance technology — with deep, hands-on SAP S/4HANA FICO experience. Demonstrated expertise in SAP S/4HANA configuration across core accounting areas: general ledger, accounts payable, accounts receivable, fixed assets, and financial close and consolidation. Experience participating in or leading at least one full-cycle SAP S/4HANA implementation — ideally on the business/functional side rather than purely technical. Strong understanding of accounting close processes, U.S. GAAP, and how ERP configuration decisions impact financial reporting. Experience with SAP master data governance, chart of accounts design, and configuration documentation. SOX experience — understanding how system controls, access management, and segregation of duties operate within SAP. Ability to translate between accounting business requirements and SAP technical configuration — comfortable working with both accountants and technical consultants. Strong communication skills — able to articulate system design trade-offs to senior finance leadership clearly and concisely. High ownership, attention to detail, and the ability to work independently without constant direction. Preferred Qualifications SAP S/4HANA certification (e.g., SAP Certified Application Associate — Financial Accounting). Experience with SAP Central Finance, SAP Analytics Cloud, or SAP BTP. CPA, CA, or equivalent professional accounting certification. Experience working at a high-growth technology or SaaS company. Prior experience working on SAP implementations. Familiarity with NetSuite (helpful for understanding the current-state processes being migrated). Experience with Databricks or other data platforms. Public accounting experience (Big 4 or equivalent). Why This Role Shape SAP from day one — you are not inheriting a legacy system. You will define how SAP works for accounting at Databricks, with the authority to ensure it is built right the first time. Challenge, don't just configure — this role exists specifically to push back on "that's how we've always done it" and ensure the implementation reflects what SAP can do, not what NetSuite did. Own the platform long-term — this is not a project role. Post go-live, you will own continuous improvement, automation, and system operations — ensuring Databricks gets progressively more value from SAP over time. Build on the Databricks platform — this is not a typical ERP role. You will define how SAP connects to the most advanced data and AI platform in the market, shaping how accounting data is used for reporting, analytics, and AI-driven automation. Few finance roles anywhere offer this combination. Work at the intersection of accounting and technology — partner with a world-class finance team, a leading SI, and Databricks' own engineering organization to build something exceptional. Grow your career — gain deep exposure to global accounting operations, finance transformation, and enterprise technology at one of the world's fastest-growing companies. text: GAQ327R240 While candidates in the listed location(s) are encouraged for this role, candidates in other locations will be considered. We're building a finance function that stays ahead of the curve — maximizing self-serve AI capabilities while driving an AI-first automation roadmap to operate at the pace Databricks demands. The Accounting Manager, Accounts Receivable, will serve as a senior individual contributor owning end-to-end technical AR accounting across global AR balances and multiple legal entities, leading multi-entity subledger consolidations as our global footprint expands. Working within a structured preparer/reviewer framework in close partnership with the broader Order-to-Cash (OTC), Revenue, and Finance Transformation teams, this high-ownership role bridges technical accounting rigor with cross-functional operational scale. Close quality, accurate management reporting, and subledger integrity are non-negotiable. Success in this role requires both strong operational execution and sound technical accounting judgment - applying U.S. GAAP to complex global receivables matters, bad debt modeling, and close accruals to ensure an audit-ready subledger. You will own a high-quality close today while directly shaping how our global receivables accounting operates tomorrow, using an AI-first automation mindset to scale our processes alongside rapid company growth. The impact you will have: Own the Global AR Month-End Close: Autonomously lead the monthly close cycle for Global AR balances, preparing end-to-end subledger-to-GL reconciliations, roll-forward schedules, unbilled revenue, deferred revenue adjustments, contra-AR, complex close accruals, and AR management reporting with clear analysis of material movements and key drivers. Technical Accounting & AFDA Modeling: Own the Allowance for Doubtful Accounts (AFDA) and Current Expected Credit Loss (CECL) accounting models; assess underlying assumptions and portfolio trends, prepare monthly provision recommendations, process approved write-offs with full audit trails, and ensure technical U.S. GAAP compliance Lead AI & Automation Adoption: Lead the identification, design, and adoption of AI and automation opportunities across AR accounting workflows, leveraging Databricks, LLMs, and advanced analytics to automate manual reconciliations, improve accrual accuracy, strengthen controls, and accelerate period closes. Maintain Balance Sheet Integrity: Own AR subledger integrity, flux analyses, variance explanations, and period-over-period movement schedules, providing clear management insights into AR trends, material movements, and key balance sheet drivers for senior Finance leadership. Drive Audit Readiness & SOX Controls: Maintain audit-ready workpapers and process documentation; serve as the primary point of contact for internal and external auditors regarding AR schedules, walkthroughs, and audit request responses. Cross-Functional Process Alignment: Partner with Billing Operations, Cash Applications, Revenue Assurance, Revenue Accounting, Corporate Accounting, and FP&A teams to validate subledger accuracy, clear unapplied balances, and reconcile AR balances. Finance Transformation & SAP Implementation: Partner with our Transformation, Engineering, and IT teams to redesign AR accounting workflows, eliminate manual routines, and drive process standardization, automation, testing, and data readiness for SAP and other systems implementations. What we look for: Experience: 6+ years of progressive AR and GL accounting experience in a mid-to-large organization, with demonstrated ownership of month-end close, AFDA/CECL, subledger-to-GL reconciliations, and AR management reporting. Credentials: CPA strongly preferred. Bachelor's Degree in Accounting or Finance. Technical Accounting: Strong U.S. GAAP judgment and ability to independently research, document, and defend accounting conclusions relating to receivables, revenue recognition alignment, accrual cut-off, contract assets/liabilities, and expected credit loss methodologies. Autonomy & Review Readiness: Proven ability to operate independently with high autonomy, producing clean, reviewer-ready workpapers within a preparer/reviewer/approver framework. Systems & ERP: Hands-on ERP experience (SAP, NetSuite, or similar) with the ability to query, reconcile, and validate data across subledger and GL modules. M&A & Integration Experience: Prior experience supporting the accounting workstream of an acquisition is a strong plus. Comfort operating in ambiguous, fast-moving integration environments with evolving data, processes, and systems is essential. The Automation Mindset: Advanced Excel proficiency (Power Query, dynamic arrays) paired with hands-on experience deploying or evaluating AI tools in a finance context; familiarity with data platforms like Databricks is a strong plus. Ownership & Mindset: High ownership, detail-oriented, fast-moving, direct communicator, and calm under pressure. Open-minded and change-oriented. Scale & Agility: High-growth technology or SaaS industry experience strongly preferred; exposure to recurring or usage-based billing models is an advantage. Public accounting background preferred.
