title: Staff Software Engineer- Search Quality
text: P-1408 The Mission We are democratizing Data and AI for every enterprise user. Our vision is a world where anyone can master their organization’s data through Apps and AI Agents. We are building the retrieval backbone for two worlds: the high-precision context layer for AI agents and the intuitive search experience for people goal is the same: instant, accurate, and actionable insight. The Role : As a Search Quality Engineer, you sit at the heart of this transformation. You aren't just building a search engine; you are building the contextual backbone of the entire company. You will own the quality of results for two distinct but deeply connected "users": The AI Agent: Optimizing the retrieval layer that allows LLMs to reason over data they weren’t trained on, ensuring they have the "ground truth" needed to synthesize accurate, high-stakes business actions. The Human User: Improving the traditional search experience so employees can find assets and answers through intuitive, high-recall interfaces. The Technical Challenge This isn't a solved problem. You will be tackling "Search" in its most evolved form: Hybrid Retrieval: Balancing traditional keyword-based search (for exactness) with semantic vector search (for intent). Dual-Optimization: Fine-tuning ranking models that satisfy both human readability and LLM-ready context. High-Stakes Accuracy: In a world of Agents, poor search quality leads to hallucinations. You will build the guardrails and relevance scoring that ensure our AI stays grounded in reality. Data Heterogeneity: Connecting the dots across structured SQL tables, unstructured docs, and real-time business metrics. Why This is the Place to Be You will have a front-row seat to the Agentic revolution. If you want to solve the hardest problems in data discovery and see your work power the decision-making of thousands of people, let’s talk. What We’re Looking For The IR Specialist: You know your way around Lucene/Elasticsearch, embeddings, and ranking algorithms. The Quality and Metrics Obsessive: You understand that "relevance" is subjective and love building evaluation frameworks (human-in-the-loop and LLM-based) to measure it. You are obsessed with relevance metrics (nDCG, MRR, Precision@K). The Bridge Builder: You’re excited to apply traditional Information Retrieval (IR) wisdom to the cutting-edge world of Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG). Strong hands-on depth: you still design systems and write production code, and can go deep on architecture for large-scale distributed services. title: Staff Technical Program Manager- Security
text: P-1489 About Databricks At Databricks, we are passionate about enabling data teams to solve the world's toughest problems; from making the next mode of transportation a reality to accelerating the development of medical breakthroughs. We do this by building and running the world's best data and AI infrastructure platform so our customers can use deep data insights to improve their business. About the Role As a Staff Technical Program Manager (TPM) for Trust & Safety Engineering, you will drive technical execution across infrastructure initiatives that protect platform integrity, user identity, and data privacy at scale. You will work directly with Security Engineering, Identity Infrastructure, Machine Learning, and Core Platform teams to design, build, and deploy systems for authentication, access control, and anomaly detection. Working embedded within engineering groups, you will translate identity protocols, privacy-by-design principles, and threat mitigation models into clear technical specifications, system dependencies, and actionable execution roadmaps. This role is focused on technical execution, resolving complex engineering dependencies, and delivering scalable systems that guarantee identity integrity and prevent platform abuse. Present program status, risks, and progress to executive and technical audiences, building trust and ensuring transparency around security posture. Ability to develop scalable solutions, optimize processes, and foster a “security by default” mindset across engineering and developer teams. Data-driven approach: skilled at defining effective metrics, surfacing insights, and using results to shape strategy and demonstrate impact. Demonstrated ability to resolve conflicting priorities and resource constraints across cross-functional teams without direct authority, establish organization-wide engineering processes, and deliver complex, multi-team roadmaps. Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to present complex technical strategies to executive engineering leaders. Experience using AI-enabled tools to accelerate program strategy, technical problem-solving, analysis, and automation. Ability to work onsite three days per week in Bellevue, Seattle, San Francisco, or Mountain View. Hands-on debugging and systems administration experience inside major public cloud boundaries (specifically AWS, Azure, or GCP platforms). Strong foundation in Linux/Unix systems engineering, containers (Docker/Kubernetes orchestration mechanics), and automated patch deployment pipelines. Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Mathematics, Engineering, or equivalent practical experience. Ability to work out of our McLean, VA secure facility, including flexibility to support 24x7 operational coverage frameworks within a SCIF environment as required. title: Staff Technical Solutions Engineer (Platform)
text: P-1378 Job Overview: We are seeking a highly skilled Frontline Staff Technical Solutions Engineer with over 12+ years of experience to join our Platform Support team. This role is pivotal in delivering exceptional support for our Databricks Data Intelligence platform, addressing complex technical challenges, and ensuring the seamless operation of our data solutions. As a frontline engineer, you will be the primary point of contact for critical issues, working closely with both internal teams and customers to resolve high-impact problems and drive platform improvements. Key Responsibilities: Frontline Support: Serve as the primary technical point of contact for escalated issues related to the Databricks Data Intelligence platform. Provide expert-level troubleshooting, diagnostics, and resolution for complex problems affecting system performance and reliability. Customer Interaction: Engage with customers directly to understand their technical issues and requirements. Provide timely, clear, and actionable solutions to ensure high levels of customer satisfaction. Incident Management: Lead the resolution of high-priority incidents, coordinating with various teams to address and mitigate issues swiftly. Conduct thorough root cause analyses and develop preventive measures to avoid recurrence. Collaboration: Work closely with engineering, product management, and DevOps teams to share insights, identify recurring issues, and drive improvements to the Databricks Data Intelligence platform. Documentation and Knowledge Sharing: Create and maintain detailed documentation on support procedures, known issues, and solutions. Contribute to internal knowledge bases and create training materials to assist other support engineers. Performance Monitoring: Monitor and analyze platform performance metrics to identify potential issues before they impact customers. Implement optimizations and enhancements to improve platform stability and efficiency. Platform Upgrades: Manage and oversee the deployment of Databricks Data Intelligence platform upgrades and patches, ensuring minimal disruption to services and maintaining system integrity. Innovation and Improvement: Stay abreast of industry trends and advancements in Databricks technology. Propose and drive initiatives to enhance platform capabilities and support processes. Customer Feedback: Collect and analyze customer feedback to drive continuous improvement in support processes and platform features. Qualifications: Experience: Minimum of 12 years of hands-on experience in a technical support or engineering role related to Databricks Data Intelligence platform, cloud data platforms, or big data technologies. Technical Skills: A deep understanding of Databricks architecture and Apache Spark™, along with experience in cloud platforms like AWS, Azure, or GCP, is essential. Strong capabilities in designing and managing data pipelines, distributed computing are required. Proficiency in Unix/Linux administration, familiarity with DevOps practices, and skills in log analysis and monitoring tools are also crucial for effective troubleshooting and system optimisation. Problem-Solving: Demonstrated ability to diagnose and resolve complex technical issues with a strong analytical and methodical approach. title: Strategy & Operations Manager - Demand Gen Programs (APJ)
text: SLSQ327R270 The Demand Gen Programs team works directly with Databricks' Sales Development and Sales leaders to build a world-class top-of-funnel engine. We give every xDR and AE the programs, plays and insights they need to turn market potential into predictable pipeline and revenue. We work where strategy, AI and the field meet. We own the programs that are moving scaled, AI-native demand gen from an experiment to the way Databricks prospects by default. We're hiring a Manager, Demand Gen programs to own demand gen programs across our APJ business. That covers markets as different as ANZ, Japan, Korea, India and ASEAN, each with its own buyers, languages and ways of selling. You'll be the APJ Sales Development organization's strategic and operational partner, and the role has three core pillars: Run demand gen programs end to end : Be a true business partner to Sales Development leadership. You'll design, align, prioritize, launch, report on and inspect the global and regional demand gen programs that run in APJ. You'll turn global programs into regional versions that work in each market, and you'll run day-to-day program management with real rigor: cadences, timelines, owners and follow-through. Agentify programs: Teach our AI demand gen platform how to prospect. You'll build agentic plays for different scenarios: defining account and contact targeting criteria, researching the messaging and content that work with APJ buyers, and curating industry- and market-specific content and use cases. You'll work with Enablement to roll these plays out to the field and make sure they're actually adopted, not just launched. Keep improving programs: Use data to judge whether programs are working. You'll define success metrics, separate what works from what doesn't, run A/B tests on messaging, targeting and sequence design, and make data-driven recommendations and pivots. You'll close the loop so that what we learn goes back into program design and into the agents themselves. Alongside Sales Development leadership, you'll work with Sales Programs, Strategy & Operations, Enablement, Marketing, Industry teams and Analytics to plan and prioritize programs, curate content and drive adoption. The ideal candidate is a self-starter with endless curiosity who works across teams to solve complex problems end to end. You're AI-fluent, operationally rigorous and opinionated about how high-volume demand gen should run. You'd rather redesign a workflow from first principles than maintain a legacy one. This is a rare chance to define what scaled, AI-native demand gen looks like at one of the fastest-growing companies in tech, and to set the blueprint for the industry. The impact you'll have Own Demand Gen Programs for all of APJ. That includes outcomes and inspection, metric design, measurement and reporting, governance, benchmarking, enablement, content strategy and change management. Shape the AI demand gen product roadmap. Bring field feedback and APJ needs to the product team. Feed the platform the content, criteria and plays that make it Databricks' core demand gen engine for both Sales and Sales Development. Drive prioritization and alignment. Run regular cadences with Sales Development and Sales Strategy leaders across APJ to gather feedback, set priorities and run programs, including SPIFs, contests, pipeline reviews and reporting reviews. Own reporting and inspection. Build the data foundation and the executive- and field-facing reporting that shows what works and what doesn't across sequences, tactics, personas, segments and markets. Turn that reporting into clear decisions, not just dashboards. Own sequence governance. Standardize, audit and manage Outreach sequences on an ongoing basis, both AI-driven and manual. Review design and effectiveness centrally, retire underperformers and scale what works. Be a force multiplier. Bring fresh thinking to old problems, build AI-powered toolkits and workflows that scale beyond you, and raise the technical bar for the whole team. Connect the pieces. Integrate demand gen programs with broader Sales, Marketing and Industry programs so the field gets one coherent motion. Own the feedback loop between the field, the programs and the platform. What success looks like First 30 days: You know the APJ Sales Development org, its leaders and the current program portfolio. You've set up a regular operating cadence with regional leadership, baselined the core program metrics, and delivered at least one quick win, such as a cleaned-up sequence library or a new inspection view. First 90 days: You've launched agentic plays tuned to APJ markets, run structured A/B tests that produced clear learnings, and set up a trusted, single source of truth for program reporting across the region. First 9 months: Scaled, AI-native demand gen is the default operating model in APJ. Coverage, conversion and xDR productivity have improved measurably, and the playbooks you built are being reused in other regions. What we look for AI fluency is non-negotiable. AI tools are part of how you work every day. You can show where they've multiplied your output. A "built something from nothing" background. Strong examples include program or GTM strategy at a hypergrowth company, owning Sales Development or demand gen programs, or consulting followed by hands-on operating experience. We want people who thrive where no playbook existed yet, and who wrote one. Exceptional attention to detail and instinct for data integrity. The role needs consistent, high-quality delivery: accurate exec-facing work, on-time delivery, honest status and zero-defect output. You spot discrepancies, trace them to the root cause, and won't ship a number you can't defend. Program ownership. You want to do the operational parts of the job, not just design them. A strategic view of high-volume demand gen. You have a point of view on how scaled coverage, AI pilots and programmatic engagement should work. You want to redefine the demand gen operating model, not maintain it. Comfort with ambiguity. The role doesn't come with a finished playbook. The right person is energized by that, not thrown by it. Technical depth. You're strong in SQL, comfortable with newer data and AI tools (Databricks SQL, Genie, custom agents), and learn fast. You can translate business needs into technical requirements and back again. A "get it done" attitude. You can set program strategy and also execute it with close attention to detail. Collaboration. You do well in collaborative teams. Regional and cross-cultural range. You've worked across APJ markets or with distributed, multicultural teams. You're comfortable working across time zones and adapting programs to local buying behavior. Excellent spoken and written communication. You present regularly and confidently to senior leaders from many cultures. You produce leader-ready decks, executive summaries and quantitative business cases. GTM tools proficiency. hands-on experience with Outreach, Salesforce or similar sales engagement and CRM tools; experience designing experiments or A/B tests; experience in data, AI or enterprise software sales. What this role isn't Not a pure strategy role. If you want to think but not execute, this isn't the role for you. The operational work (cadences, reporting, governance) isn't optional. It's where much of the impact comes from. Not a role for maintaining the current model. We need someone who will challenge how demand gen works in the age of AI and rebuild it from first principles. Not a role for anyone uncomfortable with volume, ambiguity or pace. These programs touch the entire APJ Sales Development org, and the pace of work reflects that. text: GAQ327R290 As a tax data & technology leader you will architect the redesign of our tax processes by building automation solutions and managing finance data pipelines that power our global tax organization. You will report to the Senior Director, Tax and serve as the technical anchor between the tax team and the finance data team. You will enable us to reimagine the tax function by leveraging our finance data lake to improve accuracy and efficiency of our tax processes and enable new functionality in reporting and forecasting. Importantly, you will be responsible for bridging the gap between our team's subject matter experts, our technology solutions, and all of the business data needed to support the increasing data requirements for global tax reports. This is a high-impact role that will build purposeful, reliable solutions on top of the Databricks platform and Finance Datalake to accelerate global Tax. The impact you will have: Orchestrate jobs using Databricks Jobs and Lakeflow Declarative Pipelines with built-in data validation and reconciliations that improve tax deliverables via speed & accuracy Identify, scope, and deliver AI use cases for Tax, including tax calculation automation, anomaly detection, and natural language interfaces to the financial data that supports tax Build and maintain internal tax applications (Databricks Apps, Genie Spaces, dashboards) that enable self-service for non-technical Finance stakeholders Build reports and dashboards for monthly, quarterly, and executive-level reporting Ensure data integrations are maintained and reconciled to support tax reporting & forecasting use cases Create & maintain tax calculation automations & reports are up to date (teaming with tax colleagues), accurate, and reviewable for internal and external stakeholders (e.g. external auditors) Enforce Git-based version control, pull-request reviews, and CI/CD pipelines (Declarative Automation Bundles, GitHub Actions) to satisfy SOX change management requirements Provide support during tax close and ensure timely resolution of data-related issues Partner with IT and Engineering to provide requirements and perform UAT of new systems and processes that interact with tax Establish coding, data management, and documentation standards and best practices What we look for: 6+ years of experience in tax automation, transformation, or data engineering, with at least 2 years in a tax or tax adjacent field Experience in SQL and Python for data pipeline development; experience with the Databricks platform is a strong plus Hands-on experience building and maintaining ELT/ETL pipelines connecting tax source systems (Netsuite, Salesforce, Stripe, SAP, or similar) to tax automation tools OR from those source systems into tax workflows and reports Understanding of core tax and accounting concepts including close processes, tax provision, intercompany accounting, tax compliance, and financial reporting Demonstrated ability to translate ambiguous Tax requirements into well-scoped, maintainable technical deliverables Comfortable working across both technical (Finance Data Team) and non-technical (Tax, Accounting, FP&A) stakeholders Experience with BI and data visualization tooling; ability to build Tax-facing dashboards and self-service products Familiarity with AI/ML concepts and enthusiasm for applying them to Tax workflows Nice to Have Prior experience at a high-growth SaaS or cloud infrastructure company Exposure to AI/BI tools, Genie, or LLM-powered applications Experience with Declarative Automation Bundles or CI/CD for Finance DataLake pipelines CPA, CFA, or formal finance/accounting background Why This Role You will be embedded in a Tax organization that takes data and AI seriously, reporting directly to the Senior Director of Tax, with visibility to CAO-level priorities. text: P-1584 At Databricks, we are passionate about enabling data teams to solve the world's toughest problems — from making the next mode of transportation a reality to accelerating the development of medical breakthroughs. And we're only getting started. Lakebase enables teams to deliver applications faster with an optimised database developer experience, integration with the lakehouse, and simplified operations. It provides a managed Postgres transactional layer for application state and workloads that combine operational data, analytics, and AI. You'll join as one of the founding leaders building out both the Lakebase product and our London presence. This is a Tech Lead Manager role: a hands-on technical leader who guides a small team of around five engineers while staying deep in the engineering work. You'll spend the majority of your time hands-on — driving architecture and design, solving the hardest problems in your team's projects, aligning with partner teams on dependencies, and writing code — and the rest leading and growing the engineers around you, who will report directly to you. The proxy handles all client connections and transfers every byte of query traffic, serving every data protocol: Postgres, HTTP, WebSockets, and the Data API. We route and manage large volumes of concurrent connections, solving load balancing, authentication, and data access at high throughput, with a focus on performance, observability, and reliability. Lakebase Storage — Drive continuous delivery within a team of experts in storage technology, distributed systems, and Rust. We manage the development and rollout of storage services that host millions of customer databases across dozens of regions, partnering with peer engineering teams across Databricks to co-evolve Lakebase services with our global infrastructure, and leading operational excellence in the 24/7 operation of our system. The impact you will have: Lead a small team of 5-6 engineers, owning execution and on-time, high-quality delivery. title: Technical Business Development Manager, Startup & VC Ecosystem
text: RDQ427R630 This role is in-person and Bay-Area-based by design, so you can be in the room with founders and investors. At Databricks, we are obsessed with enabling data teams to solve the world's toughest problems, from security threat detection to cancer drug development. We do this by building and running the world's best data and AI infrastructure platform, so our customers can focus on the high-value challenges central to their missions. Founded in 2013 by the original creators of Apache Spark™, Databricks has grown from a tiny corner office in Berkeley, CA, to a global organization with over 11,000 employees. Thousands of organizations, from small startups to Fortune 100, trust Databricks with their mission-critical workloads, making us one of the fastest-growing SaaS companies in the world and one of the top 5 most valuable private companies. About the Role: Databricks works with founders from the earliest days of their companies, when it is still just a team, an idea, and a lot of unproven AI. The Technical Business Development Manager for the Startup and VC Ecosystem owns the operational engine and the relationships behind that work, and the role is technical. You will run our startup program day to day, sit across from early-stage founders and talk seriously about their AI systems, produce a steady cadence of founder and investor events in San Francisco, and work hand in hand with the events teams at the venture firms whose founders we most want to reach. You will work closely with Databricks Ventures. This role is built to grow: you will start close to the program, the founders, and the events, and over time, take on more of the relationships and the strategy for how Databricks engages the startup ecosystem end-to-end. This role asks for four things that rarely sit in one person: the discipline of an operator who tracks every applicant and commitment without dropping one, the hands of a builder who is genuinely fluent in AI and can talk to a founder as a peer, the ease of someone who earns the trust of founders and the partners at the best venture firms in the country, and the judgment to turn all of that into strategy for how Databricks wins the next generation of companies. Most strong candidates have two of these, and some have three. We are hiring for trajectory: you should already be strong in the operating and the building, and hungry to grow into relationships and strategy. This is one of the rare seats where operating, building, and relationship-building are the same job. The impact you will have: Run the startup program : Own the day-to-day operations of the program, including applicant intake, evaluation, scoring, routing, and offer decisions, with precise tracking of every applicant, commitment, and outcome. Run it on AI automation built with Databricks AI tooling such as Omnigent, Unity Gateway, Agent Bricks, etc. Strong, hands-on proficiency with these tools is a requirement, not just knowing your way around them. Bring programmatic discipline : Own the trackers, the automation, the quality bar, and the follow-through so that nothing falls through the cracks. Be technical with founders : Hold real technical conversations with early-stage founders about their models, agents, data, and automation, and where Databricks and Neon fit. Earn their trust by being credible on the technology, not by pitching. Build and prototype : Build the automation and internal tooling that runs the program, and stay hands-on with the same AI tools founders use, so you can assess their technical ideas from a place of experience. This is developer relations at its most technical: close to the code and close to the builders. Assess and translate : Assess each founder's technical capability and the strength of their idea, and carry what you learn back to Product and to Databricks Ventures. Run founder and investor events : Design and run a regular calendar of founder and investor gatherings in San Francisco, including dinners, workshops, office hours, and demo-day tie-ins. Partner with the events and platform teams at leading venture firms to co-produce these gatherings, and build durable relationships with those teams that deepen over time. Represent Databricks in the ecosystem : Show up as a founder-first, technically credible presence at founder and investor events, and grow into being one of the faces of Databricks across the venture community. Grow into ownership : Work alongside Databricks Ventures on how we engage founders across the full arc of their journey, from a first look at their technology and ideas to whatever they build next, and grow into broader ownership of the startup function as you build trust and results. What we look for: This is a rare combination, and we know it. We are hiring for trajectory as much as for a finished resume: the strongest candidates are already strong on the first three and eager to grow into the rest. Genuinely technical with AI. You build. You can prototype an automation, reason about an agent architecture, and get into the details of a founder's stack without hand-waving. A programmatic operator with an obsessive eye for detail. You run complex, multi-track programs without dropping a thread. The developer-relations instinct. You earn credibility with builders by being one, and you can explain and teach hard technical ideas clearly. Comfortable around early-stage founders and investors, and ready to build relationships with top venture firms, starting with their events teams and growing toward their partners. Experience helping design and run events that people actually want to attend. Comfort switching between hands-on technical work, operational execution, and strategic thinking in the same day. Based in San Francisco. This role requires regular in-person time with founders and investors in the Bay Area. Empathy for founders and a long view of their careers. You understand that a founder's first company is rarely their last. Nice to have: a background as a founder, an early engineer, or a forward-deployed or solutions engineer; experience in B2B SaaS, AI and data infrastructure, or developer ecosystems. It is an applied team that works horizontally across the company on state of the art AI and ML and works on directly bringing that technology to the product in collaboration with product engineering teams. Pinterest is known for being a positive and inspirational place on the internet and we believe that inspiration begins with representation and belonging. The Responsible AI team is a horizontal team that collaborates across the company on various initiatives. Collaborate with cross-functional partners and Legal colleagues to address privacy issues that arise from incidents, complaints, or escalations, and help drive durable process improvements. About Pinterest Millions of people across the world come to Pinterest to find new ideas every day. It’s where they get inspiration, dream about new possibilities and plan for what matters most. Our mission is to help those people find their inspiration and create a life they love. As a Pinterest employee, you’ll be challenged to take on work that upholds this mission and pushes Pinterest forward. You’ll grow as a person and leader in your field, all the while helping users make their lives better in the positive corner of the internet. As Senior Privacy Counsel (EU), you will provide strategic, product-focused privacy counseling to help Pinterest design, build, and scale products in compliance with EU privacy requirements (including GDPR and ePrivacy). In this role, you’ll partner closely with cross-functional stakeholders—including Product, Engineering, Data, Security, Marketing, and other Legal teams—to embed privacy-by-design into the product lifecycle, guide high-impact launches, and help balance business goals with privacy compliance obligations. You’ll have the opportunity to shape and execute scalable privacy processes, including leading privacy risk assessments and supporting privacy governance across EU-facing products and features. Our new progressive work model is called PinFlex, a term that’s uniquely Pinterest to describe our flexible approach to living and working. Visit our PinFlex landing page to learn more. What you’ll do: Provide end-to-end privacy counseling, including to the Trust & Safety and Product teams on products, features, tools, and operations, from early design through launch and iteration. Advise on global privacy and data protection issues arising in the Trust & Safety context, including platform abuse prevention, content moderation, user reporting, enforcement operations, account integrity, age assurance, identity-related signals, automated decision-making, and sensitive data handling. Counsel on key legal and regulatory privacy and privacy adjacent frameworks including EU GDPR, ePrivacy, UK GDPR, CCPA, UK Children’s Code, California AADC, and other global privacy laws, with familiarity in adjacent issues involving online safety, transparency, and accountability. Lead and support privacy risk assessments, including DPIAs where applicable, and drive practical mitigations in partnership with cross-functional stakeholders. Partner closely with Trust & Safety, Product, Engineering, Security, Regulatory, and other Legal teams to operationalize privacy-by-design in systems, workflows, and investigations. Support development of scalable governance frameworks, review processes, templates, and playbooks to enable efficient and consistent privacy review. Provide guidance on third-party and vendor arrangements, including privacy terms, data protection requirements, and data sharing considerations. Advise on international data transfers for cross-border data flows, partnering with internal stakeholders and outside counsel where appropriate to support compliant transfer mechanisms and risk mitigations. Develop and improve scalable privacy workflows, templates, and playbooks to enable consistent, efficient privacy review across multiple teams and roadmaps. Collaborate with cross-functional partners and Legal colleagues to address privacy issues that arise from incidents, complaints, or escalations, regulatory inquiries, and internal investigations, and help drive durable process improvements. Leverage AI-enabled tools thoughtfully and responsibly to improve the efficiency and consistency of privacy counseling and program workflows, while maintaining appropriate legal oversight and quality control. What we’re looking for: Qualified to practice law in the jurisdiction where you reside with a minimum of 10 years of experience. Demonstrated experience providing privacy counseling in a fast-paced environment to Trust & Safety and Product teams, with the ability to translate legal requirements into clear, practical guidance for business, product, and technical teams. Experience leading or materially supporting DPIAs/privacy risk assessments, and driving cross-functional mitigations to enable launches while managing risk. Experience with privacy product counseling on ads in the tech sector, as well as advising on commercial matters, including reviewing, drafting, and negotiating data processing agreements (DPAs) and advising on related data protection terms, a significant plus. Excellent judgment, strong ownership, and the ability to operate independently on sensitive and high-stakes matters. Strong written, verbal, and interpersonal communication skills, with the ability to influence and build alignment across cross-functional teams. Demonstrated ability to manage multiple projects and competing priorities with independence, sound judgment, and attention to detail, and a practical, solutions-oriented approach. Demonstrated ability to use AI and other technology tools effectively and responsibly and identify practical opportunities to improve effectiveness, or willingness to learn. Experience navigating complex, multi-jurisdictional legal and compliance issues for a technology company or similarly dynamic environment preferred. You’ll align People strategies with business priorities and support organizational health, leadership effectiveness and growth across a complex and evolving set of markets. In this high-impact role, you’ll lead core HRBP work across talent, organizational effectiveness, leadership coaching and change, while also serving as a key representative for Pinterest with the French Works Council. This experience is essential, as you will help ensure thoughtful, compliant and people-centered partnership in France while connecting local market needs with global People strategies. Serve as a trusted advisor to senior leaders on organizational health, leadership capability, team effectiveness, employee experience and change. Lead regional talent priorities across France, the UK and Germany, including workforce planning, talent reviews, succession planning, leadership development, career growth and performance management. Drive organizational effectiveness through organization design, team structure, decision-making clarity, change readiness and scalable operating models. Guide leaders through restructuring, business evolution and other complex change efforts while balancing business needs, employee experience and risk. Represent Pinterest with the French Works Council, including building trusted relationships, preparing for consultations, partnering cross-functionally on required information and helping leaders navigate Works Council processes thoughtfully and effectively. Provide expert guidance on employee relations matters, local employment practices and market-specific considerations across France, the UK and Germany in close partnership with Employee Relations, Legal and other People teams. Partner with Global HRBPs and Centers of Excellence to bring regional insights and local context to global People strategies, programs and decisions affecting the region. Use workforce insights, data and AI-enabled tools to improve decision-making, scale People practices and strengthen organizational effectiveness. Apply sound judgment, verification and responsible data stewardship to AI-assisted work. Help bring Pinterest’s culture and values to life across the region in ways that are inclusive, meaningful and locally relevant. title: American Tech Fellowship
text: A World-Changing Company Palantir builds the world’s leading software for data-driven decisions and operations. By bringing the right data to the people who need it, our platforms empower our partners to develop lifesaving drugs, power decisions on the battlefield, locate missing children, and more. Applications for the January 2027 cohort are open now through December 11, 2026. The Program In the 20th century, America pioneered mass production. We built the Arsenal of Democracy and won the war. Then we left this mighty Arsenal to rust. Silicon Valley, a product of Heartland work ethic, turned its back on the American worker. It's time to reawaken the giant. The same spirit of practical innovation that enabled America to dominate the previous century lives on in every American factory, workshop, and garage today. Some fear the proliferation of Artificial Intelligence, but we see the opportunity for a technological and industrial renaissance. Palantir is launching the American Tech Fellowship to arm Americans with the skills to deploy cutting-edge software in the workforce. You will have an opportunity to explore and build on Palantir's Artificial Intelligence Platform (AIP) and earn a professional certification in its use. Exceptional performers will earn an opportunity to interview for a role at Palantir or partner companies, where you can use your newfound skills to contribute to the revival of American industry. This fellowship is about more than careers. It's about restoring the promise that hard work and determination can still change your life in America. It's an investment in American excellence, and evidence of our belief that America's greatest builders are still to be discovered. The American worker, given the right tools and opportunity, remains our competitive advantage. It's time to prove it. The Role In this fellowship, you'll participate in a comprehensive training program with our partner, Ontologize , to level up your technical skills on Foundry and AIP. You'll learn how to deploy Palantir's advanced software to solve tough problems in enterprise settings and have the opportunity to engage directly with Palantir engineers and leadership. The fellowship runs for 12 weeks, beginning on January 13, 2027. You are expected to attend live virtual sessions on two weeknights each week. We will also have optional sessions once a week and office hours throughout the duration of the program. Expect to spend 10 to 15 hours per week on instruction and project work throughout the fellowship. This program provides valuable training to participants and is unpaid. The window for submitting American Tech Fellowship applications is now through December 11, 2026. What We’re Looking For We want builders: people who are hungry to learn whatever it takes to succeed and aren't afraid to roll up their sleeves and make it happen. You might be that kind of person if you've taught yourself, or been the local go-to, in one or more of these areas: Software, data, or automation General-purpose programming languages such as Python, C/C++, C# / .NET, Rust, Go, Java, TypeScript/JavaScript Data science applications such as SQL, MATLAB, Simulink, R, Julia, Excel + VBA Process improvements like instrumenting, automating, or optimizing how things run Prototyping—i.e., testing ideas iteratively instead of waiting for perfect specs What We Value Show us where you've flexed that builder's mindset. That could look like: Formal study in computer science, electrical/mechanical/control systems engineering, physics, applied math, data science, mechatronics, robotics, or a related field Experience solving real problems in settings such as a factory floor, a warehouse or logistics hub, a hospital or clinic, a construction site, field service, energy or utility operations, the military, a small business, or a garage shop, especially if you automated, instrumented, or optimized a process Startup, maker-space, or hackathon projects that blended hardware and software, such as retrofitting equipment, building a sensor network, or deploying an edge AI model Publications, patents, or open-source contributions in software, data, automation, or related technical fields If you've got the fire to learn and you've built something that moved the needle, you're the kind of American worker we designed this fellowship for. Backgrounds in skilled trades, manufacturing, and field work, as well as in clinical or business settings, are welcome. What We Require 2+ years of hands-on work experience in a technical setting or engaging in on-the-job technical processes Backgrounds in computer science, data science, physics, and engineering domains are preferred, though no formal degree is required. title: Backend Software Engineer - Data Connectors
text: A World-Changing Company Palantir builds the world’s leading software for data-driven decisions and operations. By bringing the right data to the people who need it, our platforms empower our partners to develop lifesaving drugs, forecast supply chain disruptions, locate missing children, and more. The Role The Connectivity team builds the software that connects Palantir’s platform to customer systems. Our connectors integrate databases, enterprise applications, cloud storage, web services, and streaming systems, enabling customers to bring data into Foundry and write back to their operational systems. From large datasets to real-time events and user-driven interactions, these connections underpin the applications and AI workflows customers build with Foundry and AIP. You’ll build and maintain Foundry’s first-class connector suite and the shared infrastructure behind it. You’ll work across the stack, taking ownership of connector implementations, developer SDKs, and the systems that build, test, distribute, and run our connectivity software. A central part of this work is evolving and scaling a large, established codebase. You’ll move integrations from bespoke infrastructure onto shared platform capabilities, design SDKs that enable other teams and customers to build integrations independently, and safely retire older implementations. You’ll also build observability and diagnostic tools that help users understand, monitor, and troubleshoot their connections. You’ll own improvements from design through production and use what you learn from operating connectors to strengthen the platform they share. Technologies We Use Java and Python for connectors, backend services, and developer SDKs Open-source technologies like Kafka, Kubernetes, Flink, Debezium, Iceberg Industry-standard build tooling, including Gradle and GitHub Shared job orchestration, streaming, serverless execution, and compute deployment platforms Core Responsibilities Build and maintain Foundry’s first-class connectors, improving performance and extending support for imports, exports, change data capture, interactive queries, and writeback as external systems and customer needs evolve. Improve the infrastructure that builds, tests, packages, and distributes connectors and shared libraries, including tooling across our connector monorepo. Design and maintain connectivity SDKs for internal teams and end users, with clear APIs, documentation, testing utilities, and development workflows that make integrations easy to author and maintain. Collaborate with product teams to integrate connector execution with job orchestration, streaming, and serverless platforms. Lead incremental migrations onto shared infrastructure, manage compatibility, and retire older implementations while preserving the workflows customers depend on. Develop reusable security frameworks and tooling that make secure connectivity a consistent part of connector development and execution. Debug production issues and performance problems across the stack, turning recurring support problems into durable fixes, automated tests, and better observability. Establish shared testing frameworks, compatibility checks, and release practices that keep a large connector portfolio reliable and maintainable. Help prepare and maintain Palantir connectivity software for open-source use, including its APIs, packaging, documentation, and contributor experience. What We Value An ownership mindset and a high bar for correctness, security, and automated testing, including responsibility for how software behaves in production. Pride in building and maintaining integrations over time, including the detailed work required to keep them reliable as upstream systems change. Engineering judgment that balances delivering new capabilities with simplifying existing systems and reducing operational burden. Empathy for developers and end users, reflected in usable SDKs, clear configuration, actionable errors, and useful diagnostics. Curiosity about unfamiliar systems and persistence in debugging problems across languages, APIs, services, networks, and execution environments. What We Require 4+ years of professional software engineering experience developing external system connectors, with depth in areas such as developing batch and streaming data ingestion systems, third-party integration development, or monorepo and asset distribution frameworks. Operating on top of these technologies alone does not qualify. Deep expertise in Gradle, including developing custom plugins, managing multi-project builds, and optimizing build performance. Demonstrated ability to diagnose complex reliability and performance problems and improve systems through measured, incremental changes. Strong written and verbal communication skills and the ability to work effectively across teams, incorporate feedback, and hold a high bar for quality. By bringing the right data to the people who need it, our platforms empower our partners to develop lifesaving drugs, forecast supply chain disruptions, locate missing children, and more. The Role Palantir's defense product vertical builds mission-critical products for the modern warfighter. We provide a complete ecosystem where customers can securely integrate and visualize their data, and build sophisticated, full-fledged programs such as common operating pictures, alert-triaging inboxes, and resource allocation planning tools driven by rich-ML models. Our customers use our defense offering to perform rich analyses that drive core operations within their organizations - these programs are relied upon for daily operations in the command centers and battlefronts of militaries across the world. Backend Software Engineers at Palantir build software at scale to transform how organizations use data. Our Software Engineers are involved throughout the product lifecycle, from idea generation, design, prototyping, and production delivery. You will collaborate closely with technical and non-technical teammates to understand our customers' problems and build products that solve them. We encourage movement across teams to share context, skills, and experience, so you'll learn about many different technologies and aspects of each product. Engineers work autonomously and make decisions independently, within a community that will support and challenge you as you grow and develop, becoming a strong technical contributor and engineering leader. Your day-to-day workflow will vary, adapting to the requirements of our users and the technical challenges that arise. One day, you may find yourself collaborating with other engineers to architect a new system that enables a novel workflow, the next you could be fine-tuning performance to enable low-latency operational outcomes. Our Product Development organization is made up of small teams of Software Engineers. Each team focuses on a specific aspect of a product and work collaboratively to build cross functional capabilities, streamline user workflows and continuously improve our software's efficiency and reliability. We're hiring engineers who are passionate about solving real-world problems and empowering developers and end-users to do their work optimally. If you’re motivated to develop reliable, performant, scalable systems and design robust APIs and primitives, please join us. Some examples of product work you could work on are: Build for high-scale, collaborative, geospatial workflows ( Gaia ) Design sophisticated frameworks to enable complex workflows across applications in a single workspace Develop the next generation of real-time collaborative tooling and data-analysis solutions ( Secure Collaboration ) Core Responsibilities Architecting, developing, and maintaining high-performance, scalable backend services that underpin our our operational data and AI systems Maintaining high coding standards through the development of guidelines, active participation in code reviews, and fostering a culture of continuous improvement and knowledge sharing among your team Building robust APIs for use by front-end developers and interfacing external systems, and collaborating with front-end developers to integrate user-facing elements with server-side logic Designing efficient data structures and algorithms to manage large-scale and high throughput data Optimizing applications for speed and scalability through performance analysis Actively improve user workflows by collaborating with cross-functional teams, ensuring seamless experiences across product boundaries and a cohesive user experience Technologies We Use Different backend languages, including Java, Rust, Python and Go Distributed systems technologies such as Kafka, Cassandra, Elasticsearch and Spark Docker and Kubernetes for containerization and orchestration Industry-standard build tooling, including Gradle and GitHub What We Value A deep understanding of server-side logic, efficient data handling, and distributed systems Strong focus on creating user-oriented workflows and solutions, crossing product boundaries to deliver cohesive and solid user workflows that ensure a seamless and intuitive user experience Experience building high-quality software in a fast-paced CI/CD development environment Ability to work collaboratively in teams of technical and non-technical individuals and understand how technical decisions impact the people who will use what you're building Skill and comfort working in a constantly evolving environment with dynamic objectives and iteration with users What We Require Experience in designing and developing features and improvements, as well as supporting and maintaining, live backend systems In-depth understanding of data structures, system architecture, API development for microservices frameworks, distributed systems and other backend-related concepts and best practices Engineering background in Computer Science, Mathematics, Software Engineering, Physics or similar field Strong coding skills with demonstrated proficiency in programming languages, such as Java, C++, Python, Rust, or similar languages Strong written and verbal communication skills and ability to iterate quickly with teammates, incorporating feedback and holding a high bar for quality Eligibility and willingness to obtain a US Security clearance Salary The estimated salary range for this position is estimated to be $135,000 - $200,000/year. Total compensation for this position may also include Restricted Stock units, sign-on bonus and other potential future incentives. Further note that total compensation for this position will be determined by each individual’s relevant qualifications, work experience, skills, and other factors. This estimate excludes the value of any potential sign-on bonus; the value of any benefits offered; and the potential future value of any long-term incentives. Our benefits aim to promote health and wellbeing across all areas of Palantirians’ lives. We work to continuously improve our offerings and listen to our community as we design and update them. The list below details our available benefits and some of the perks that can be enjoyed as an employee of Palantir Technologies. Benefits • Employees (and their eligible dependents) can enroll in medical, dental, and vision insurance as well as voluntary life insurance • Employees are automatically covered by Palantir’s basic life, AD&D and disability insurance • Commuter benefits • Relocation assistance • Take what you need paid time off, not accrual based • 2 weeks paid time off built into the end of each year (subject to team and business needs) • 10 paid holidays throughout the calendar year • Supportive leave of absence program including time off for military service and medical events • Paid leave for new parents and subsidized back-up care for all parents • Fertility and family building benefits including but not limited to adoption, surrogacy, and preservation • Stipend to help with expenses that come with a new child • Employees can enroll in Palantir’s 401k plan Life at Palantir We want every Palantirian to achieve their best outcomes, that’s why we celebrate individuals’ strengths, skills, and interests, from your first interview to your longterm growth, rather than rely on traditional career ladders. Paying attention to the needs of our community enables us to optimize our opportunities to grow and helps ensure many pathways to success at Palantir. Promoting health and well-being across all areas of Palantirians’ lives is just one of the ways we’re investing in our community. Learn more at Life at Palantir and note that our offerings may vary by region. In keeping consistent with Palantir’s values and culture, we believe employees are “better together” and in-person work affords the opportunity for more creative outcomes. Therefore, we encourage employees to work from our offices to foster connectivity and innovation. Many teams do offer hybrid options (WFH a day or two a week), allowing our employees to strike the right trade-off for their personal productivity. Based on business need, there are a few roles that allow for “Remote” work on an exceptional basis. If you are applying for one of these roles, you must work from the state in which you are employed. If the posting is specified as Onsite, you are required to work from an office. If you want to empower the world's most important institutions, you belong here. Palantir values excellence regardless of background. We are proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer for all, including but not limited to Veterans and those with disabilities. Palantir is committed to making the application and hiring process accessible to everyone and will provide a reasonable accommodation for those living with a disability. If you need an accommodation for the application or hiring process , please reach out and let us know how we can help. Please note that you will never be asked to submit a payment or share financial information to participate in our interview process. If you suspect that you've been contacted by a scammer, we recommend you cease all communication with the individual and consider reporting them to the relevant authorities, such as the US FBI Internet Crime Complaint Center (IC3) . If you would like to understand more about how your personal data will be processed by Palantir, please see our Privacy Policy .

title: Backend Software Engineer - Infrastructure
text: A World-Changing Company Palantir builds the world’s leading software for data-driven decisions and operations. By bringing the right data to the people who need it, our platforms empower our partners to develop lifesaving drugs, forecast supply chain disruptions, locate missing children, and more. The Role Software Engineers at Palantir build software at scale to transform how organizations use data. Our Software Engineers are involved throughout the product lifecycle, from idea generation, design, prototyping, and production delivery. You will collaborate closely with technical and non-technical teammates to understand our customers' problems and build products that solve them. We encourage movement across teams to share context, skills, and experience, so you'll learn about many different technologies and aspects of each product. Engineers work autonomously and make decisions independently, within a community that will support and challenge you as you grow and develop, becoming a strong technical contributor and engineering leader. Our Product Development organization is made up of small teams of Software Engineers. Each team focuses on a specific aspect of a product. Our infrastructure teams are responsible for the lowest layers of our software stack, often focused on database technologies, distributed systems, large scale data systems, security, and application infrastructure. As a Software Engineer on infrastructure working on our Foundry platform, you'll contribute high-quality code to underpin Palantir Foundry and Gotham with performant, secure, and scalable building blocks, enabling products deployed to the most important institutions in the public and private sector. You'll build the foundational capabilities that power our products used by research scientists, aerospace engineers, intelligence analysts, and economic forecasters, in countries around the world. We’re hiring engineers who are passionate about solving real-world problems and empowering both developers and end-users to work optimally. If you’re motivated to develop reliable, performant, and scalable systems, and to design robust APIs and primitives, this role offers the opportunity to make a significant impact on our products and the people who use them. Frontline Foundry Software Engineers may be offered the opportunity to Frontline, an exclusive program unlike any other. This unique, short-term assignment involves being embedded with customers, allowing you to work directly with users and gain firsthand insight into how our products are used and the challenges our customers face. Unlike traditional engineering roles, Frontline immerses you in complex, ambiguous problems, empowering you to deliver impactful solutions across some of the world’s most important industries and institutions. Some of our most successful products were built on the factory floor, addressing real-world problems for the world's most important institutions. These products were developed by some of our most successful product engineers, who began their careers in roles aligned with Frontline responsibilities, gaining a deep understanding of both our technology and our customers. Frontliners operate across a broad spectrum of responsibilities, much like a startup CTO. They work in small teams to own the end-to-end execution of high-stakes projects. This spectrum ranges from discussing architecture and building custom web apps to conducting workshops with users and strategizing with customer executives. No two days are alike, as each day is diverse and impactful. By witnessing how customers engage with Foundry and experiencing these pain points firsthand, you’ll gain unique insights that feed directly back into our development process, helping to refine and enhance our products. Core Responsibilities Building a performant search and indexing ecosystem for complex granularly permissioned data Contributing to open-source data processing libraries, integrating the latest innovations to achieve performance gains Building the distributed systems that power large scale compute workloads, orchestrating and efficiently scheduling hundreds of thousands of containers every hour Designing architecture and opinionated APIs to keep application developers on the happy path Tracing and performance observability in high scale distributed microservice architectures Building reliant, performant, and scalable systems for storage, auth, or asset serving to enable other product teams to build robust applications without deep domain expertise in the underlying systems Automating the deployment, management, and operations of complex distributed systems like Cassandra, Elasticsearch, Kafka, and more across different environments Technologies We Use Different backend languages, including Java, Rust, and Go Open-source technologies like Cassandra, ElasticSearch, Spark, Kafka, Kubernetes, Flink Industry-standard build tooling, including Gradle and GitHub What We Value Demonstrated ability to collaborate and empathize with a variety of individuals. Able to iterate with users and non-technical stakeholders and understand how technical decisions impact them. Ability to learn new technology and concepts, even without in-depth experience. Experience developing and managing highly-available distributed systems is beneficial, but not required. Bias towards quality and thoughtful about edge cases (“anything that can go wrong will go wrong”); writes code that is defensive against all possibilities. Builds solutions and APIs with users in mind while maintaining a high engineering bar. Seeks to centralize and abstract complexity away from our users in order to expose simple, powerful APIs for consumers. Active US Security clearance, or eligibility and willingness to obtain a US Security clearance is beneficial, but not necessary. What We Require Engineering background in Computer Science, Mathematics, Software Engineering, Physics or similar field. Strong coding skills with demonstrated proficiency in programming languages, such as Java, C++, Python, Rust, or similar languages. Familiarity with storage and data processing systems, cloud infrastructure, and other technical tools. Strong written and verbal communication skills and ability to iterate quickly with teammates, incorporating feedback and holding a high bar for quality. Salary The estimated salary range for this position is estimated to be $135,000 - $200,000/year. title: Deal Team - Business Affairs
text: A World-Changing Company Palantir builds the world’s leading software for data-driven decisions and operations. By bringing the right data to the people who need it, our platforms empower our partners to develop lifesaving drugs, forecast supply chain disruptions, locate missing children, and more. The Role Our Deal Team members collaborate with multiple Palantir teams to proactively engage with existing and prospective commercial customers, leading the structuring and negotiation of deal terms so that Palantir can continue to drive positive impact in the world. As a member of the Deal Team, you will partner closely with Palantir’s Legal, Finance, Sales, and Engineering teams to drive deal execution and support our growth efforts at scale, while directly owning the development and negotiation of commercial terms for commercial customers. You will use your expertise to unite our customer’s needs and considerations with our company’s strategy, using your creativity to identify the right commercial structure and approach for each customer. You will also utilize your understanding of the business landscape and build relationships with internal partners, increasing the visibility of deal progress and forecasting impact across all levels of our organization, from analysts to C-suite executives. In this role, you will also support various special projects that arise at our fast-paced, mission-focused company. We’re a team that values both creativity and teamwork. Whether operating solo or collaboratively, we endeavor to achieve great results on challenging, time-sensitive deal discussions and projects. You'll be given open ended objectives and expected to find ways to turn them into outcomes. By focusing on the broad vision without losing sight of the details, you'll bring large and multi-phase deals to successful completion while prioritizing team outcomes over individual wins. You are able to deliver complex commercial contract and deal information in an understandable way, and can manage high touch stakeholders in a constantly shifting landscape. You are ready to become an expert on the intricate details of deal negotiations and contracts that enable Palantir to implement its cutting-edge technology to solve real-world problems. Core Responsibilities Collaborate with Sales counterparts to develop the pricing terms and commercial structure for each commercial customer. Lead negotiations of commercial terms during the contracting process, guiding communications as appropriate for the situation. Draft materials in support of deal negotiations, including pricing proposals, term sheets and order forms, while advising the business on commercial structure implications including revenue impact and timing. Cooperate with internal Legal, Finance, Sales and Engineering teams to drive deals to execution, providing trusted guidance for navigating negotiations and procurement processes and maintaining engagement throughout the customer lifecycle to develop and negotiate commercial terms for renewal and up-sell opportunities. title: Deployment Strategist
text: A World-Changing Company Palantir builds the world’s leading software for data-driven decisions and operations. By bringing the right data to the people who need it, our platforms empower our partners to develop lifesaving drugs, forecast supply chain disruptions, locate missing children, and more. What We're About At its core, this role is about uncovering dots and—without knowing the shape they form—figuring out how to connect them. Our customers come to us with a hunch that the only way to protect their troops, manufacture high-quality products, structure effective healthcare policies, or deliver aid to refugees safely is to make better use of their data. Deployment Strategists are responsible for turning that hunch into reality. If you believe in the transformational power of data and technology and in your own ability to bring that power to bear against complex problems, we want to meet you. What We Do As a Deployment Strategist, you'll work as part of a driven and creative team of Engineers, Product Designers, and other Deployment Strategists to deploy software against the most challenging problems our world faces. Your mission is to synthesize disconnected streams of thought into a cohesive understanding of what the most important problem is, what the data means, what the product needs, what users are motivated by, and where the impact could be. Deployment Strategists are do-ers who immerse themselves in our customers' most intricate workflows, partner with customer teams and explore the data, and dive into the product landscape to enable us to scale. A select number of Deployments Strategists may also be deployed to Palantir internal teams and problems. In this role, the problems you'll tackle will require a curious and analytical mindset, a sharp intuition for product, and a strong degree of user empathy to ultimately empower our customers to make better decisions. No two days are the same, but as a Deployment Strategist you can expect to: Go onsite and meet with customer analysts to understand the critical questions they need to answer and locate their biggest pain points. Identify relevant datasets through deep engagement with customer problems and workflows, and work with Forward Deployed Engineers to integrate the data into a stable and extensible pipeline. Work with the customer to build bespoke workflows for new user groups. Lead training sessions to ensure that the product is meeting user needs, and to ensure it is being used widely enough to have concrete impact on our partners' operations. Present the results of our work and proposals for future work to audiences ranging from analysts to C-suite executives. Embed with our Software Engineering and Product Design teams to incorporate what you saw in the field into cross-Palantir product offerings. Build and deliver demos to new and existing customers. Scope out potential engagements in new industries and in increasingly expanding locations around the world. What We Value We value team members who aren’t satisfied with surface-level answers. We value the desire to dive into the details of the data because that’s the core of our work. And we value low ego because the outcome matters more than who gets the credit. Extraordinary ability to take on open-ended problems in unstructured environments. Adaptive and introspective; willing to learn, teach, lead and follow. Ability to travel 25 – 75% required. Varies by location and team. Experience with programming, scripting or statistical packages (e.g. Python, R, Matlab, SQL) is a plus. What We Require Ability to read, write, and speak fluent business Korean and English is a requirement. We partner with the most important institutions in the world to transform how they use data and technology. Our software has been used to stop terrorist attacks, discover new medicines, gain an edge in global financial markets, and more. What We're About At its core, this role is about uncovering dots and—without knowing the shape they form—figuring out how to connect them. Our customers come to us with a hunch that the only way to protect their troops, manufacture high-quality products, structure effective healthcare policies, or deliver aid to refugees safely is to make better use of their data. Firma, która zmienia świat W Palantirze dążymy do rozwiązywania najważniejszych i najbardziej wymagających problemów na świecie. Wierzymy, że tworzenie oprogramowania umożliwiającego podejmowanie decyzji przez ludzi jest najlepszym sposobem na osiągnięcie tego celu. Współpracujemy z najważniejszymi instytucjami na świecie, aby przeobrazić sposób, w jaki wykorzystują dane i technologię. Nasze oprogramowanie było wykorzystywane m.in. do powstrzymania ataków terrorystycznych, odkrywania nowych leków, zdobywania przewagi na globalnych rynkach finansowych. Kogo szukamy Nasi klienci przychodzą do nas z przeczuciem, że jedynym sposobem na ochronę ich żołnierzy, wytwarzanie wysokiej jakości produktów, budodwanie skutecznych struktur dla opieki zdrowotnej lub zapewnianie pomocy uchodźcom jest lepsze wykorzystanie danych. Deployment Strategist jest odpowiedzialny za przekucie tego przeczucia w rzeczywistość. Praca polega przede wszystkim na odkrywaniu wskazówek i określaniu sposobu ich połączenia na podstawie dostępnych informacji. Jeśli wierzysz w transformacyjną moc danych i technologii oraz w swoją zdolność do wykorzystania tej mocy do walki ze złożonymi problemami, chcemy poznać Cię bliżej. Co robimy Jako Deployment Strategist będziesz pracować w ramach zaangażowanego i kreatywnego zespołu inżynierów, projektantów produktów i innych Deployment Strategists, aby wdrażać oprogramowanie w odpowiedzi na najtrudniejsze problemy, z którymi mierzy się świat. Twoja misja polega na syntetyzowaniu oddzielnych strumieni przemyśleń w celu zrozumienia jaki problem jest najważniejszy, co mówią o nim dane, czego potrzebuje produkt, co motywuje użytkowników i na jakiej płaszczyźnie można wywrzeć największy wpływ. Deployment Strategists to osoby, które zagłębiają się w najbardziej skomplikowane procesy i zespoły naszych klientów, oraz analizują dane i wkraczają w środowisko produktów, aby umożliwić nam odpowiednie skalowanie.. Problemy, z którymi będziesz się mierzyć, będą wymagały dociekliwości i analitycznego myślenia, intuicji w zakresie budowania technicznych produktów oraz silnej empatii względem użytkowników, tak aby ostatecznie umożliwić naszym klientom podejmowanie lepszych decyzji. Określona liczba Deployment Strategists może również zostać wcielona do wewnętrznych zespołów Palantira pracujących nad wyzwaniami naszej firmy Każdy dzień jest niepowtarzalny, ale jako Deployment Strategist możesz oczekiwać, że: • Spotkasz się bezpośrednio z analitykami klienta, aby zrozumieć kluczowe pytania, na które muszą odpowiedzieć, aby zlokalizować najważniejsze problemy w swoich organizacjach. • Będziesz identyfikować istotne zbiory danych poprzez głębokie zaangażowanie w problemy i procesy klientów oraz współpracę z inżynierami pierwszej linii (Forward Deployed Engineers) w celu integracji danych w obrębie stabilnego i skalowalnego procesu. • Będziesz współpracować z klientem, aby stworzyć dopasowane do niego sposoby pracy dla nowych grup użytkowników. • Będziesz prowadzić sesje szkoleniowe, aby upewnić się, że produkt spełnia potrzeby użytkowników i jest wykorzystywany na skalę, mającą konkretny wpływ na działalność naszych partnerów. • Będziesz przedstawiać wyniki naszej pracy i propozycje dotyczące przyszłej pracy odbiorcom, począwszy od analityków, a skończywszy na kadrze kierowniczej najwyższego szczebla. • Dołączysz do naszych zespołów inżynieryjnych i projektowania produktów, aby uwzględnić obserwacje z terenu w ofercie produktów Palantira. • Będziesz tworzyć i przedstawiać prezentacje nowym i obecnym klientom. • Będziesz rozszerzać potencjalne zaangażowanie w nowych branżach i w coraz bardziej rozwijających się lokalizacjach na całym świecie. Co sobie cenimy • Członków zespołu, którzy nie są zadowoleni z powierzchownych odpowiedzi. Chęć zanurzenia się w szczegóły danych –to jest podstawa naszej pracy. A także skromność, ponieważ wyniki mają większe znaczenie niż kto zdobędzie za nie uznanie. • Niezwykłą zdolność do rozwiązywania otwartych problemów w nieustrukturyzowanych środowiskach. • Adaptacyjne i introspektywne podejście; chęć uczenia siebie i innych, gotowość do kierowania, jak i podążania za liderami. • Wymagana możliwość podróżowania na poziomie 25-75%. Wymóg ten różni się w zależności od lokalizacji i zespołu. • Plusem będzie dodatkowe doświadczenie w zakresie programowania, pisania skryptów lub używania pakietów statystycznych (np. Python, R, Matlab, SQL). Wymagania: • Biegła znajomość języka polskiego. • Poświadczenie bezpieczeństwa lub możliwość do jego uzyskania. Życie w Palantir Chcemy, aby każdy z pracowników firmy Palantir osiągał najlepsze wyniki, dlatego doceniamy mocne strony, umiejętności i zainteresowania poszczególnych osób od pierwszej rozmowy kwalifikacyjnej po długoterminowy rozwój, zamiast polegać na tradycyjnych drabinach kariery. Zwracanie uwagi na potrzeby naszej społeczności umożliwia nam optymalizację naszych możliwości rozwoju i pomaga zapewnić wiele dróg do sukcesu w Palantir. Promowanie zdrowia i dobrego samopoczucia we wszystkich obszarach życia pracowników firmy Palantir to tylko jeden ze sposobów inwestowania w naszą społeczność. Dowiedz się więcej na stronie Życie w Palantir i pamiętaj, że nasza oferta może się różnić w zależności od regionu. Wierzymy, że postępowanie zgodne z wartościami i kulturą firmy Palantir sprawia, iż pracownicy „lepiej współpracują ze sobą”, a praca osobista daje możliwość bardziej kreatywnych wyników. Dlatego zachęcamy pracowników do pracy w naszych biurach, aby wspierać powiązania i innowacje. Wiele zespołów oferuje opcje hybrydowe (dzień lub dwa dni w tygodniu pracy w domu), dzięki czemu nasi pracownicy mogą uzyskać odpowiedni kompromis dla swojej osobistej produktywności. W zależności od potrzeb biznesowych istnieje kilka ról, które pozwalają na „zdalną” pracę w wyjątkowych warunkach. Jeśli ubiegasz się o jedno z tych stanowisk, musisz pracować w mieście i kraju, w którym jesteś zatrudniony. Jeśli oferta w ogłoszeniu jest określona jako „na miejscu”, musisz pracować w biurze. Jeśli chcesz wzmacniać najważniejsze instytucje świata, jest to miejsce dla Ciebie. Palantir ceni doskonałość niezależnie od pochodzenia. Dokładamy wszelkich starań, aby proces składania aplikacji i zatrudniania był dostępny dla wszystkich, oraz zapewnimy odpowiednie udogodnienia osobom z niepełnosprawnością. Jeśli potrzebujesz udogodnienia w procesie aplikacji lub zatrudnienia, skontaktuj się z nami i daj nam znać, jak możemy Ci pomóc. Pamiętaj, że nigdy nie zostaniesz poproszony(-a) o przesłanie płatności lub udostępnienie informacji finansowych w celu wzięcia udziału w naszym procesie rekrutacyjnym. Jeśli podejrzewasz, że skontaktował się z Tobą oszust, zalecamy zaprzestanie wszelkiej komunikacji z taką osobą i rozważenie zgłoszenia jej odpowiednim organom, takim jak amerykańskie Centrum ds. Nos clients viennent nous voir parce qu’ils pensent que la seule façon de protéger leurs collaborateurs, de fabriquer des produits de haute qualité, de structurer des politiques de santé efficaces ou d’aider les réfugiés en toute sécurité est de mieux utiliser leurs données. Si vous croyez au pouvoir transformationnel des données et de la technologie et à votre propre capacité à mettre ce pouvoir au service de la résolution de problèmes complexes, nous voulons vous rencontrer.
